splits.module_summary:
`src/sandbox/launch.rs` (8,880 lines: 1–6,171 production, 6,172–8,880 the single inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`) is the whole launch pipeline plus four unrelated verbs that happen to reach a cage. It is declared `mod launch;` at `src/sandbox/mod.rs:20` and re-exported at `src/sandbox/mod.rs:141-145` (`SessionHeader, app, attach, detach_log_path, effective_lock_target, gc, parse_session_header, run, run_mise, stop, superseded_reclaimable_hint, upgrade_mise_packages, upgrade_provision_steps`). Four more items cross the module boundary directly: `pub(super) session_housekeeping`/`shared_store_gc` (read by `src/sandbox/projects.rs:164,293,657,729`) and `pub(super) seccomp_argv`/`status_code` (read by `src/sandbox/task.rs:1154,1221`, `src/sandbox/taskpool.rs:512`, `src/sandbox/resolver.rs:221`, and named in a doc link at `src/sandbox/spec.rs:221`).

splits.rationale:
The file is not one machine; it is one machine (`Prepared` → `build` → cage) with four unrelated verbs bolted on, and the project's own stated criterion for carving a module out already covers two of them. `src/sandbox/mod.rs:114-117` says `projects` is "Kept apart from `launch` because it shares no state with the launch pipeline". `attach` (2609-2896) and `stop` (2904-3055) meet that test exactly: 499 lines that never touch `Prepared`, never call `build`, never resolve a config, and enter namespaces bwrap already made. `gc` (1794-2473) and the two `sbx upgrade` rolls (1023-1764 + 5651-5717) are batch/maintenance drivers that borrow the launch machinery rather than being part of it. Together those three clusters are ~2,700 production lines that a reader auditing "what reaches bubblewrap" must page past.

The split is cheap because Rust privacy runs downward: everything private in `launch/mod.rs` (`Prepared`, `prepare*`, `observation_flags`, `may_exec_replace`, `prebuilt_ctx`, `mise_tools`, `seed_project_store`) stays reachable from every child with no annotation at all, and each child's `use super::*;` inherits the parent's import block exactly the way today's `mod tests { use super::*; }` at 6174 already does. Only child→parent and child→sibling edges need `pub(super)`, and I have enumerated every one of them below.

What I am **not** proposing: carving up `build` itself. Its 1,728 lines are a single linear assembly whose ~40 locals (`wraps`, `extra_binds`, `gui_env`, `notify_wiring`, `brokers`, `egress_env`, `tcp_plan`, `signer_ring`, `fs_masks`/`fs_decoys`, `task_socket`) are consumed in three places at the end (`extra_cage_env` 4952, `binds::build_spec` 5028, the `LaunchGuard` literal 5183). Extracting the GUI-hole block (4618-4801) or the provisioning prologue (3489-3854) would move 8-10 values across a signature and split the one surface `src/sandbox/mod.rs:4-7` asks a security review to audit in one place. `build` moves **whole** into `launch/build.rs`; that sharpens the seam (the function that stands up a cage, alone with the helpers only it uses) instead of dissolving it. `launch/build.rs` therefore stays the largest file at ~2,700 lines, and that is the honest floor.

The real cost is not cyclic dependencies — Rust modules may reference each other freely, so there is no cycle risk in any arrangement here — it is three mechanical sweeps: (a) ~174 `super::X` references inside the moved ranges must be rebased to `crate::sandbox::X` (counted per module below); (b) ~20 intra-doc links must gain a path prefix, and `mise run rustdoc` fails loudly on each one it misses rather than silently dropping it; (c) two source-scanning tests and two `docs_coverage.rs` allowlist entries name the file by path and must be repointed. All three are enumerable, and the compiler/rustdoc/test guards catch every miss.

proposed_modules.purpose: The launch entry points and the prerequisites everything else in the directory shares: `Prepared`, the `prepare*` chain, the launch-mode decision, and the `run`/`app`/`mise` verbs. Also holds the three provisioning primitives `build` and the gc sweep both need, precisely because a parent's private items are visible to every child without an annotation.

splits.other_observations:
**A duplicated driver that only becomes visible once the two rolls sit together.** `upgrade_mise_packages` (1226-1485) and `upgrade_provision_steps` (1525-1659) are the same 130-line control flow twice: compute groups → compute the dot-leader `width` from `home.name()` (1310-1315 vs 1563-1568) → per group, skip `NetworkPolicy::Isolated` with an identical `roll_line(name, width, "network \"none\" — skipped")` (1322-1334 vs 1576-1588) → `cfg.warnings.clear()` + `prep.cfg = cfg` → `build` → on `Err` print "failed to launch" and `failed += 1` (1354-1366 vs 1600-1612) → `run_captured` → `drop(guard)` → report → tally → recap coloured by `failed > 0 / ran.is_empty()` (1470-1484 vs 1648-1658). Only the group type, the cage command, and the success line differ. A `trait RollGroup { fn name(&self); fn label(&self); fn runtime(&self); fn cfg(&self); fn command(&self, prep) -> Vec<OsString>; fn report(&self, code, out) -> String; }` with one `fn run_groups(...)` driver would collapse it. I would do this **after** the move, not as part of it: it is a behaviour-preserving refactor of ~260 lines that is far easier to review when both copies are in one 1,060-line file than when they are 300 lines apart in an 8,880-line one.

**Three duplicated cage-command preambles, safely collapsible inside `cage.rs`.** `run_status` (5601-5616), `run_captured` (5631-5641), `exec` (5751-5766) and `supervise` (5779-5786) each repeat the identical trio `seccomp_argv(spec)?` → `netns::holder_wrap(bwrap, argv, spec.netns_dummy.as_ref())` → `cgroup::wrap(&holder_prog, holder_argv, limits, &spec.cage_slug)`. A single `fn cage_command(bwrap, spec, limits) -> io::Result<(PathBuf, Vec<OsString>, Vec<File>)>` states it once; the returned `Vec<File>` is load-bearing (`seccomp_argv`'s doc at 5718-5722 says the memfds must outlive the exec), so the signature has to hand them back rather than drop them. This is a genuine four-way collapse, it is entirely local to the proposed `cage.rs`, and the existing tests at 6574-6673 and 8329-8353 already cover the argv it produces.

**Two near-identical prebuilt walks that should NOT be collapsed.** `build` (3545-3606) and `equip_for_gc` (2400-2445) both iterate `prebuilt::DIRECT_ORDER` then `RESOLVE_ORDER` over `prep.cfg.packages`, pushing roots. `src/sandbox/prebuilt.rs:643` already notes the pairing. But the resolve halves differ on the security-relevant point: `build` calls `provision_resolve` (which *runs* the profile's resolve command in a hermetic cage and may touch the network), `equip_for_gc` calls `provision_resolve_pinned` and its comment at 2432-2434 says gc "must never run the resolve command or touch the network". Factoring them into one function parameterised by a `run_command: bool` would put that guarantee behind a boolean argument. Leave them apart; the duplication is the cheaper of the two costs.

**Vestigial visibility, tightened by the move rather than worked around.** `LaunchGuard` (3308) and all thirteen of its fields are `pub(crate)`, but grep across `src/` finds no user outside `launch.rs`; moving it into `build.rs` as `pub(super)` is a real narrowing. Conversely `AppOutcome` (763) must stay `pub(crate)` — `src/cli/app.rs:72,74` reads `.learned` and `.code` without naming the type.

**Section ordering is already broken today, which is part of the argument.** Four functions that exist only to serve `upgrade_mise_packages` (`mise_transitions` 5651, `mise_up_to_date` 5664, `roll_line` 5670, `mise_roll_recap` 5681) sit 4,000 lines below it, wedged between `run_captured` and `seccomp_argv`; `wrap_mise_equip` (5419) sits 4,200 lines from the `MISE_EQUIP_VERB` (1160) whose pairing its doc explains; `equip_announcement` (1163) sits with the roll but is only ever called by `build` (4052). The proposal puts each beside the thing it belongs to, which is why several modules take two disjoint line ranges rather than one contiguous block.

**Suggested order of execution**, so each step is independently reviewable and `mise run ci` is green between them: (1) promote the test helper `resolved` to `src/testutil.rs`; (2) `git mv src/sandbox/launch.rs src/sandbox/launch/mod.rs` with no other change (proves the path-only edits — `docs_coverage.rs:914-915` and the two `include_str!` targets at 6429 and 7641); (3) `startup.rs` (zero `super::` rewrites, largest self-contained test block); (4) `session.rs`; (5) `detach.rs`; (6) `equip.rs`; (7) `roll.rs`; (8) `reclaim.rs`; (9) `cage.rs`; (10) `build.rs` last, since it is the residue. Run `mise run rustdoc` after every step — it is the only guard that catches a doc link that stopped resolving, and it fails the build rather than dropping the link silently.

splits.rationale:
The decisive fact is not size, it is subject. This file holds **two different lenses** that share nothing but one notification descriptor.

Counting non-test lines: the **open/content lens** (`[fs] scan`, whose pure half is `src/open_policy.rs`) is ~1490 lines — `OpenName`/`open_name` 676–741, the open branch of `handle_notif` 879–961, `serve_open`..`park_open` 1218–1662, `open_flags`/`open_mode`/`open_resolve` 1711–1819, `open_args` 2020–2039, and the whole 2064–2827 block. The **exec gate** (`[proc]`, pure half `src/proc_policy.rs`) is ~364 lines: `exec_verdict` 619–674, the exec branch 962–1030, `caller_chain`/`refusal_errno` 1032–1101, `PendingExec` 1833–1979, `exec_args` 2041–2062. The 115-line module header describes only the second one; the open lens appears in it exactly twice, in passing (lines 85, 107), and has no module-level prose anywhere.

The seam between them is unusually exact, which is what makes this a mechanical split rather than a hopeful one. `Deciding` (745–756) has seven fields; the entire open branch of `handle_notif` (879–961) touches exactly two of them — `cx.open` (lines 900, 912, 933) and, via `open_name`, `cx.undecidable`. It never touches `ring`, `notifier`, `pending`, `policy` or `overlay`. So the open half can be lifted behind a single call `handle_open(notif_fd, req, dirfd, path_addr, lens: Option<&OpenLens>, undecidable: &Undecidable)` with **no back-reference to `Deciding` at all** — no cycle, not even a conceptual one.

Underneath both lenses there is a genuinely policy-free mechanism layer that is currently interleaved with them: the ioctl ABI and the four answer forms (158–190, 1103–1216, 1821–1831), the fd handoff (2829–2939), and the parked-target reads plus per-syscall register decoding (1664–1819, 1981–2062). Nothing in that layer calls into either lens — it is a clean leaf, and it already carries its own tightly-scoped unit tests (`ioctl_codes_match_the_kernel_abi`, the four `each_*_form_*` tests, `the_shortest_open_how_the_kernel_accepts_is_the_whole_first_version`, `the_handoff_control_buffer_is_aligned_for_the_header_it_is_read_as`).

Answering the framing directly: policy-decision / mechanism / reporting **are** separable here, but not symmetrically. The mechanism separates cleanly. The *open* policy decision separates cleanly. The *exec* policy decision does not earn a module — it is 126 lines and every one of its tests needs the `DecidingParts` harness (5469–5512) that lives with the shim-driven tests, so it stays in `mod.rs` beside `handle_notif`. Reporting separates only halfway: the `Undecidable` counters and the teardown report are a real unit, but the `diag::warn` calls are deliberately emitted at the site that knows (549–554: "Counted at the read and not by its caller, deliberately"), and a reporting module that hoovered those up would dissolve a documented decision.

What must **not** be split: the supervisor state machine `supervise`/`accept_handoff`/`recv_loop`/`handle_notif`/`close_supervision` (743–1030, ~288 lines) is one machine with one invariant — the single listener never blocks — and the `Spec`-side seam is elsewhere entirely. It stays whole in `mod.rs` together with the lifecycle it is documented by.

The crate already has this exact shape twice: `src/sandbox/proxy/` (16 flat children, `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;` in `proxy/tests.rs`) and `src/sandbox/control/` (children plus `pub(crate) use capture::*;`). Re-exporting the seven `pub(crate)` items from `mod.rs` means **zero call-site changes outside the module** — `crate::sandbox::proc_enforce::Refusal` and friends keep their paths, and `src/proc_policy.rs:6` / `src/open_policy.rs:6`, which link `[`crate::sandbox::proc_enforce`]`, keep resolving.

**Two `super::` hazards specific to a directory module.** (1) Code: `super::sanitize` at 1888, 2609, 2628 must become `crate::sandbox::sanitize` once those lines live one level deeper; the four `super::` uses inside `start_inner` (415, 418, 420, 434, 436, 437) are untouched because `start_inner` stays in `mod.rs`, where `super` is still `sandbox`. Write bare `mod open_lens;` etc. and put every `//!` inside the child file.

**Rejected: an `exec_decide.rs`.** `exec_verdict` (619–674), `caller_chain` (1032–1101) and `refusal_errno` (1079–1101) are only 126 lines, they need `Deciding` (a child→parent `use super::Deciding` back-edge, legal but the one place the layering would stop being one-way), and every test that drives them — `an_execve_whose_target_cannot_be_read…` 5561–5592, `a_caller_whose_program_is_not_a_name…` 5626–5702 — needs the `DecidingParts` harness that stays in tests.rs. Leave them in `mod.rs` beside `handle_notif`, which lands `mod.rs` at roughly 760 lines: header 1–115, `SHIM_CAGE_PATH`/`NOTIF_SOCK_CAGE_PATH` 152–156, the lifecycle 268–528, the supervisor 743–878 and 962–1030, the exec decision 619–674 and 1032–1101, plus `mod` declarations and the `pub(crate) use` re-exports that keep the external surface at its current paths.

**Dead structure.** Line 192 is a section banner, `// ── the in-cage shim ──`, with nothing under it — the shim is a separate binary in `proc-shim/`. Delete it rather than carry it into a child.

**Over-broad visibility, independent of the split.** `send_resp` (1822) is `pub(crate)` with exactly two callers, both in this file (1141, 1149) and both of which end up in the same new module. `OpenLens` (2393) is `pub(crate)` and has no user outside `proc_enforce` at all. Both can be tightened while moving, at no cost to any call site.

**A latent bug the split surfaces rather than causes.** `PARKED_OPENS` (1580) is a process-wide `AtomicUsize` against a process-wide `PARKED_OPEN_CAP` of 64, but a single sbx process can run more than one supervisor: `start_for_task` (387) exists precisely because "a session serving two invocations at once" is a real state (377–386). Two concurrent supervisors therefore share one flood cap, so a cage that parks 64 FIFO opens starves its sibling's opens into `EACCES`. `ADDFD_UNAVAILABLE` (1154), `OPENAT2_UNAVAILABLE` (2258) and `UNNAMEABLE_OPEN_SAID` (741) are also process-global; for the first two that is correct (they record a kernel property), for `UNNAMEABLE_OPEN_SAID` it means the second launch in a process says nothing. Worth a separate look — the cap plausibly belongs on `OpenLens`, which is already per-launch and already holds the other per-launch state (`cache`, `mounts`).

**Ordering, if this is done incrementally.** notify.rs → target.rs → cagepath.rs are pure leaves and can each land alone, each a self-contained commit with its own tests, before any of the larger moves. open_lens.rs and open_serve.rs should land together (the `handle_open` extraction is what makes both clean). pending.rs, overlay.rs and report.rs are independent of all of the above and of each other. tests.rs should be last, after every `pub(super)` it needs already exists.

First, every sibling except `view.rs`/`manage.rs`/`safety.rs` opens with `use super::*` (`types.rs:5`, `validate.rs:14`, `load.rs:7`, `secrets.rs:6`, `tasks.rs:42`, `tests.rs:5`), and they reach mod.rs's *private* items through it — `validate.rs` alone uses `is_zone_name`, `is_valid_uri_scheme`, `is_valid_nixpkgs_source`, `classify_entries`, `parse_http2_hosts`, `mode_from_parent`, `unknown_notify_event`, `parse_duration`, `sort_forward`, `parse_forward_entry`, `NetGroups`, `AppHomeScope`. The existing `#[cfg(test)] use secrets::{…}` at line 54 is proof the pattern already carries load in this crate.
splits.rationale:
This is not one cohesive state machine. It is one 954-line state machine (`fn resolve`, 1640–2593) surrounded by six or seven subjects that share nothing but `&mut Vec<String> warnings` and `TrustState`. Concretely: the app resolver (`resolve_app`, 3270–3935) takes twelve explicit parameters and touches no local of `resolve`; the package-locator grammar (`parse_backend`/`classify_backend`/the six URL validators/the five charset validators) is a set of pure leaf predicates whose main consumers are *outside* `config` entirely (`src/sandbox/{deb,tarball,binary,appimage,prebuilt,nixhub}.rs`, `src/store.rs:1668`); the `[plugin.<name>]` attachment pass (1349–1612) is a self-contained two-entry-point walk. None of these is entangled with the layering engine — they are called from it and return.

The cost is bounded and mechanical, and lower than it looks, for one reason: the file's intra-doc links cluster along exactly the seams I propose. Of the 60-odd bare links in the file, `apply_packages` (×6), `apply_tools` (×5), `is_valid_deb_url` (×5), `TARBALL_RESOLVE_SENTINEL` (×3), `apply_flakes`, `apply_resolvers`, `parse_backend`, `strip_fetch_scheme`, `is_valid_tarball_url` all sit inside the tool block and stay intra-module if it moves as one piece; `refuse_untrusted`, `Gate::refuse`, `untrusted_reason`, `TRUST_DROP_MARKER`, `dropped_binds_warning` all sit inside the gate block; `apply_plugin_host_config`(×2) and `apply_plugin_host_config_to_secrets`(×2) inside the plugin block. The `Resolved::merge_app` (×9 as `[…](Resolved::merge_app)`), `Resolved::apply_override`, `Resolved::validate_override` links are method-qualified and resolve wherever the `impl` block lives. Cyclic dependency is not a risk category in Rust — modules in one crate may reference each other freely — so the only real hazards are (a) a name that stops being glob-visible and (b) a bare doc link crossing a new boundary. Both are enumerable, and I enumerate them per module below.

Why "worthwhile" and not "strongly recommended": `fn resolve` stays 954 lines under every proposal. It is a single linear pass over ~60 accumulator locals, and there is no way to break it up that does not either invent a `ResolveState` builder (which would put a mutable god-struct where explicit locals are today) or thread twenty `&mut` parameters through sub-functions. Leave it whole and say so. Likewise `merge_app` (669–794) reads nearly every field of `Resolved` and belongs beside it. So the split takes the file from 5846 to roughly 2450 lines, not to 1200 — a real improvement, not a transformation. The three highest-value, lowest-risk moves are #1 (apps), #2 (tools) and #6 (gate); they are independent of each other and can land as three separate reviewable commits. Modules #3–#5 and #7 are worth doing but carry less benefit per unit of diff, and nothing is lost by deferring them.

That module's header (overrides.rs:45–48) already states the seam in prose: 'This module only *collects and merges* the inputs into one overlay; the authoritative application onto a resolved configuration is [`super::Resolved::apply_override`]'. This turns that paragraph into a file boundary. Do NOT fold it into overrides.rs — that would dissolve the stated seam and push that file past 3100 lines.

All three are `pub(crate) fn` methods on `Resolved`; Rust permits inherent `impl` blocks for a type in any module of the defining crate, and a method path (`Resolved::apply_override`) is independent of which file the block lives in. That is also what keeps overrides.rs:46–48's two doc links (`[`super::Resolved::apply_override`]`, `[`super::Resolved::apply_override_channel`]`) resolving with no edit. Doc links inside the move: `[`build_override_scalars`]`, `[`Resolved::apply_override`]`, `[`Resolved::validate_override`]`, `[`Resolved::apply_override_channel`]` are intra-cluster or method-qualified; `[`crate::sandbox::effective_lock_target`]` and `[`Provenance::Override`]` are absolute / glob-resolved. The one thing to watch is that `apply_override` calls fifteen mod.rs helpers (`apply_env`, `apply_binds`, `apply_packages`, `apply_seccomp`, `apply_devices`, `apply_fs`, `apply_ssh_agent`, `union_forward`, `union_devices`, `union_ssh_agent`, `overlay_limits`, `mark_limit_origins`, `enforce_secret_posture`, `canonicalize_binds`, `sbx_control_plane_roots`) plus five `validate::*` — all arrive through `use super::*`, but `apply_packages` now lives in tools.rs, so mod.rs's private `use tools::{apply_packages, …}` (module #2) is a prerequisite. Inline tests: none — the override tests live in tests.rs:7515–8126 and reach `apply_override` through `Resolved`, so they need no edit. Cycles: none. Naming note: the file cannot be called `override.rs` (reserved word) and must not be called `overrides.rs`.

splits.other_observations:
**A real doc-comment defect the split would force you to fix.** `ResolvedApp`'s doc comment is broken at src/config/mod.rs:503–522. Line 503 reads `/// An app's resolved overlay over the sandbox baseline: the command to run plus the extra` — and then line 504 starts `BundleProvision`'s own doc (`/// One bundle's install step, as the fold hands it to a launch…`), so `ResolvedApp`'s opening sentence is rendered as part of `BundleProvision`'s documentation, and `ResolvedApp`'s doc (519–522) now begins mid-sentence with the lowercase fragment `/// environment, binds, packages, network posture, and credentials it declares — each`. `BundleProvision` was clearly inserted into the middle of `ResolvedApp`'s doc block. rustdoc does not complain (both links resolve), so `mise run rustdoc` is silent about it. Fix while moving `ResolvedApp` to `apps.rs`: line 503 rejoins 519–522, and `BundleProvision` keeps 504–510.

**A second `#[cfg(test)]` sibling is already precedent for splitting the suite.** `src/config/catalogue_tests.rs:4–8` states the rule in prose: 'Kept apart from [`super::tests`], which exercises the resolution engine… A contributor adding a shipped profile has no reason to open the engine's suite, and one changing the engine has no reason to page through these.' That is the same argument for subdividing `tests.rs`.

**Should tests.rs (11317 lines, 341 `#[test]`s) follow the split? Yes — but as a separate change, after the source split, and on the same topic axis.** It costs nothing today (it is already out of mod.rs, and `cargo test --lib config::tests::<filter>` already targets it), so it is not urgent; and the real work is not moving tests but extracting fixtures, which is independent of everything above. Specifics if you do it:
- The clusters are visible but *not contiguous*, which is the main cost. Egress groups 65–583; app overlay / brokers / limits / `merge_app` 584–3986; env+binds 3988–4799; packages/backends/resolvers/libs 4800–6069; nixpkgs/network/gui/forward/fs/devices/ssh_agent 6070–7062; secrets+resolver plugins 7088–10167 — but one-shot overrides are wedged inside that span at 7515–8326, and notify+overrides reappear at 10797–11317. Any split has to re-sequence, not just cut.
- Fixture builders are scattered across at least six sites and shared across clusters: 65–190 (`validate_network` shim, `raw`, `declare_groups`, `net_table_defaults`, `net_field`, `make_groups`), 584–826 (`ro_bind`, `rw_bind`, `raw_packages`, `raw_nixpkgs`, `raw_network*`, `raw_gui`, `raw_forward*`, `same_forwards`, `raw_devices`, `raw_ssh_agent`, `raw_seccomp`, `raw_limits`, `raw_app`, `raw_with_app`, `a_header_secret`), 2382–2500, 3988–3992 (`pkg`, `get`), 7088–7200, 7363–7377 (`vhs`, `resolve_no_plugins`, `zoned`), 8328–8430, 8682–8810. These want one `src/config/tests/fixtures.rs` that every topic file does `use super::fixtures::*;` against.
- One sharp edge: tests.rs:60–78 defines a **shadowing shim** `fn validate_network` that deliberately shadows the glob-imported real function so 'the many bare 3-argument calls read as before'. If the suite becomes `mod tests { mod fixtures; mod groups; mod apps; … }`, that shim must live in `fixtures` and be glob-imported by exactly the files that want the shadowing — and any file that calls the real four-argument `validate_network` must not import it. Get this wrong and tests silently compile against the wrong function.
- Suggested shape, mirroring the source split one-for-one so a contributor changing `apps.rs` knows to open `tests/apps.rs`: `fixtures.rs`, `groups.rs`, `apps.rs`, `tools.rs`, `binds_env.rs`, `postures.rs`, `secrets.rs`, `plugins.rs`, `overrides.rs`, `invariants.rs` (the last for the cross-cutting `every_*_names_itself_in_its_refusal` family at 10342–10796, which deliberately spans every field and should not be filed under any one topic).

**A deliberate anti-DRY seam to respect.** `expand_bind_path`'s doc (mod.rs:4209–4220) ends with 'Do not merge the two behind one helper', about its intentional divergence from the resolver-plugin `allow_paths` expander over a literal `$` past the head. Whatever else moves, that function keeps its doc verbatim.

**A collapsible near-duplication, offered but not recommended.** The global-layer field reads in `resolve` (1806–1960: network/proc/notify/gui/forward/limits/seccomp/devices/fs/ssh_agent, each 'validate → assign → stamp origin') are structurally parallel to the global-app-layer reads in `resolve_app` (3402–3560), and the project halves (`resolve` 2190–2470 vs `resolve_app` 3640–3800) already share `Gate`. A `Gate`-shaped 'trusted-by-location layer' helper could collapse perhaps 120 lines. I would not do it: the two differ in the mode-inheritance parent they pass and in `T` vs `Option<T>` slots, and forcing them together would need a generic that obscures which of the two a reader is looking at — the exact readability the current duplication buys.

**No dead code found** in mod.rs. Every private item has at least one caller inside `config`; the closest thing to an orphan is `is_valid_uri_scheme` (5400), whose sole caller is `validate::validate_open` — reached only through `use super::*`, which is worth knowing before anyone 'tidies' it."

Coupling between clusters 2/3/5/6/7/8 is essentially nil: I grepped every private symbol and found no call crossing a cluster boundary except the three dispatchers and `write_session_header{,_line}`. No shared mutable state, no state machine, no borrowed lifetimes crossing a boundary (`PendingGroup<'a>` and `capture_of<'a>` are internal to their own clusters). Every test also falls cleanly inside exactly one cluster; not one test straddles two.
splits.rationale:
This is not one cohesive state machine — it is six near-independent verb subsystems concatenated, with a two-function shared surface. The evidence for the seam being real rather than cosmetic: (a) not a single private symbol is called across the six clusters; (b) the 1642-line test block partitions with zero straddling tests; (c) the current layout already fails to keep a cluster together — `net_pending_drain_and_save` (3274–3449) sits between the rule-write functions and 2200 lines from `net_pending_answer` (its only caller, at line 817), and `write_session_header*` (680–725) sits buried inside the pending block. The repo already has this shape elsewhere (`src/config/`, `src/sandbox/control/`, `src/allowlist/`), so the pattern needs no invention.

I stop short of "strongly recommended" because the cost is real and not zero: 12 items must widen from private to `pub(super)`, six new `use crate::{…}` headers must be derived exactly right (an over-copied import is an `unused_imports` warning, and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` is a hard gate), and the module header at lines 1–12 has to be rewritten into a map of the children while keeping the "plumbing stays at the crate root" paragraph that is still true. Nothing here is broken today; the win is navigation, review-diff locality, and `cargo test --lib cli::net::logs` granularity.

THE ONE HARD CONSTRAINT — verified, and it dictates the shape: two source-scanning guards read `src/cli` with a NON-recursive `std::fs::read_dir` filtered to `extension == "rs"` (`src/cli/mod.rs:968-975` in `dispatch_heads`, and `src/help.rs:3728-3735` in `dispatched_alias_pairs`). Nothing under a `src/cli/net/` directory is ever scanned. Consequences:
- `src/cli/mod.rs:1101-1116` asserts that every help path with child pages has a dispatcher head. `["net"]`, `["net","pending"]` (pages at `src/help.rs:2515,2536,2582`) and `["net","groups"]` (pages at `src/help.rs:2260,2275`) all qualify, so moving `net_cmd`, `net_pending` or `net_groups` into a child file fails `every_routed_subcommand_is_named_by_its_parents_page` with "has subcommand pages but the scan found no dispatcher for it".
- `src/help.rs:3678` `DISPATCHERS` hard-codes `("net.rs", "net_cmd", &["net"])`, and `body_lines` (`src/help.rs:3699-3712`) panics unless `fn net_cmd(`/`pub(crate) fn net_cmd(` starts at column 0 in a file literally named `net.rs`. Moving it also breaks the reverse check at `src/help.rs:3813-3820` for the declared alias `(&["net"], "log", "logs")` (`src/help.rs:3108`, dispatched at `src/cli/net.rs:52`).

So the split MUST be `src/cli/net.rs` (kept as the module root, Rust-2018-style, edition is 2024 per `Cargo.toml:4`) plus a `src/cli/net/` directory — NOT `src/cli/net/mod.rs`. `net.rs` retains the three dispatchers and the shared session-header writer. Declare children as bare `mod pending;` etc. with NO outer `///` on the `mod` line: `mise.toml:95-98` documents that a doc comment on a `mod` declaration merges with the child's own header and moves resolution into the declaring module's scope, which `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --document-private-items` (`mise.toml:102`) then flags. `src/config/mod.rs:17-27` and `src/sandbox/control/mod.rs:35-36` are the in-repo precedent for exactly that.

Cyclic-dependency risk is nil in the Rust sense (module cycles compile), and the design has none anyway: it is a strict tree. Children reach `write_session_header{,_line}` via `use super::…` — legal without any visibility change, because a private item is visible in its defining module AND all descendants. Only the 12 dispatched entry points widen, to `pub(super)`.

splits.other_observations:
Four concrete cleanups found while mapping, all independent of the split (do them before or after, not during — a move-only commit is far easier to review):

1. DUPLICATED INTERVAL PARSER. `src/cli/net.rs:1309-1321` (inside `parse_log_args`) re-implements `crate::interval_seconds` (`src/main.rs:251-263`) byte-for-byte, including all three error strings: "`--interval` needs a value in seconds", "invalid interval `{}` — expected a whole number of seconds", "interval must be at least 1 second". The file already imports `interval_seconds` and uses it correctly twice — `parse_watch_args` at line 234 and `parse_live_args` at line 320. Replace the whole arm with `Some("-i") | Some("--interval") => v.interval_secs = interval_seconds(it.next())?,`. 13 lines to 1, with no behaviour change and no test change (`parse_log_args_reads_every_flag_and_rejects_bad_input` at 4253 asserts those exact messages and keeps passing).

2. THREE NEAR-IDENTICAL GATHER FUNCTIONS. `collect_pending` (85–103), `collect_flows` (336–353) and `collect_logs` (1363–1388) are the same 15-line shape: call `sandbox::control::{list_all|flows_all|log_all}`, `retain` on `session_pids_for_app` when `app` is set, then pair with `pending_session_context`. They differ only in the control call and, for `collect_logs`, two extra bool args. A generic `fn scoped<T>(data_dir: &Path, app: Option<&str>, list: impl FnOnce(&Path) -> Vec<T>, pid_of: impl Fn(&T) -> u32) -> (Vec<T>, Vec<(u32, PathBuf, String)>)` would collapse them. I would NOT put it in the crate root — it is a `cli::net` concern; it belongs in `src/cli/net.rs` beside `write_session_header`. Worth doing only if you take the split, because otherwise the three stay adjacent-ish and the abstraction buys little. Note each carries a distinct, load-bearing doc comment (`collect_logs`'s 1363–1372 explains why the muted ring is always folded in) — that prose must survive on the call sites, not be collapsed into the generic.

3. SEVEN COPIES OF THE CWD BLOCK. `src/cli/net.rs:1119-1123, 2169-2175, 2562-2568, 3006-3011, 3027-3032, 3078-3083, 3308-3313` each hand-roll `match std::env::current_dir() { Ok(d) => d, Err(e) => { diag::error(&format!("sbx: cannot read the current directory: {e}")); return ExitCode::FAILURE; } }`. `crate::config_cwd()` (`src/main.rs:266-272`) already does this and is used 9 times in `cli/app.rs`, `cli/config.rs` and `cli/upgrade.rs`. CAVEAT that makes this not a pure win: `config_cwd` uses a bare `eprintln!`, while `diag::error` (`src/diag.rs`) routes through `highlight(msg, &Palette::for_stream(…))`, so backticked spans in the message get colored on a TTY. The message text is identical, but switching would silently drop that highlighting on seven paths. Either accept that, or change `config_cwd` to call `diag::error` (which would change the 9 existing call sites' output too, so it needs its own look).

4. AN ARGUMENT-PARSING FAMILY THAT NEVER FORMED. `net_pending_list` (144–170), `net_stats` (1090–1109) and `net_rules` (2123–2167) each hand-roll the same `--app`/`-a` + `--json` walk with slightly different error text ("sbx: `--app` needs an app name" vs "sbx: net stats: `--app` needs an app name" vs "sbx: net rules: `--app` needs an app name"), while `parse_watch_args`, `parse_live_args` and `parse_log_args` are pure, testable parsers returning `Result<T, String>`. The three inline walkers are the odd ones out and are the only arg paths in the file with no direct unit test. I am flagging this rather than proposing it: converting them means choosing one error-prefix spelling, which is user-visible text and possibly asserted in `tests/`. It is a deliberate follow-up, not part of a mechanical split.

Nothing in this file is dead. I checked every private symbol; all 68 have at least one non-test caller.

splits.rationale:
The file contains two programs that do not talk to each other, and the seam is provable rather than aesthetic: no call edge crosses it (verified by grepping every function name against the whole file), and the import sets are disjoint (`trust::` and `cli::confirm::*` live entirely below 2349; `allowlist::DEFAULT_*`, `net_mode_word` and `short_rev` entirely above it). The `#[cfg(test)]` module partitions along the same line with no shared fixture: `sample_config_view()` (3238–3349) is called only by `render_config` tests (3354–4147), and the four edit-verb tests (3112–3236, 3946–3962) share nothing with them. After the split three of the five files contain no `diag::`, no `std::process`, no filesystem call — they are pure `&View -> String` presenters, which is exactly what `render_config`'s own doc at 1644–1647 claims ("a pure presenter over `config::view` … a future front-end can render the same model differently"). The split makes a stated design property physical instead of conventional.

The cost is small and enumerable: ~19 items go from private to `pub(super)` (crate-invisible outside `cli::config`), two rustdoc links need a `use crate::config;` carried into the new files, and one prose reference in `src/main.rs:601` needs its path updated. `src/cli/mod.rs:8` needs no edit, because the crate already uses `mod.rs`-style directory modules (`src/config/`, `src/sandbox/`, `src/plugins/`, `src/allowlist/`, `src/sandbox/control/`).

Why "worthwhile" and not "strongly recommended": the split does not make the file small. `render.rs` still lands at ~2760 lines (~2160 after the test-fixture cleanup in `other_observations`), because the baseline document genuinely is one cohesive thing — `render_config` (1644–1702) is a single ordered list of section calls and the code says at 1655–1657 that the order is load-bearing, so cutting the sections into "collections" vs "whole-view" groups would put the document's structure in two places to save nothing. That residual is the honest floor. If appetite is limited, take **only the render/edit cut** (modules 1+2 below merged as `mod.rs`, module 5 as `edit.rs`): that is one file move, ~9 visibility changes, zero rustdoc risk, and it removes 908 lines and the entire `trust`/`confirm`/`ScopeArgs` import surface from the render side.

splits.other_observations:
**The net.rs comparison — the most valuable finding.** `src/cli/net.rs` (5168 lines) and `src/cli/config.rs` (5004) are the same size and both flat, so the interesting divergence is internal, and it is in argument parsing.

net.rs has established a pattern for option-heavy verbs: a named args struct plus a pure parser returning `Result<T, String>`, with the handler mapping the error once. Three instances: `struct WatchArgs` (220–224) + `parse_watch_args` (228–250), `struct LiveArgs` (304–312) + `parse_live_args` (313–338), `struct LogView` (1252–1276) + `impl LogView` (1278–1284) + `parse_log_args` (1290–1372). The rationale is stated in the code — `parse_watch_args`'s doc at 225–227 and `parse_log_args`'s at 1286–1289 both read "Pure (no I/O), so every reject path is unit-testable". The payoff is visible in the tests: `parse_watch_args_defaults_and_overrides` / `_rejects_bad_input` (3783–3822), `parse_live_args_*` (3823–3863), `parse_log_args_reads_every_flag_and_rejects_bad_input` (4253–4328). The handler is then trivial — `net_logs` (1450–1457) is six lines of parse-or-exit.

config.rs has adopted none of it. `config_show` (89–204) carries six flags and two conflict rules and parses them inline, returning `ExitCode` from inside the loop, so no reject path is reachable from a unit test. The consequence is measurable: the `--app` + source conflict at 141–158 has **no test anywhere** — `grep -rn "does not combine with" tests/ src/` returns exactly one hit, the source line itself. Only `set_show_source` (62–87) was extracted, and only because someone wanted to test it (3964–3972).

Be honest about the limit of this comparison: net.rs is not uniform either — `net_pending_list` (144–166), `net_stats` (1086–1110) and `net_rules` (2116–2168) still inline-parse exactly like `config_show`. So the finding is not "net is clean, config is dirty"; it is that net has a house pattern for its heaviest verbs and config has never taken it up, despite `config show` being precisely that shape.

Concrete follow-on, independent of the split and cheap: add `struct ShowArgs { json, details, app, source }` + `fn parse_show_args(args: &[OsString]) -> Result<ShowArgs, String>` to the new `src/cli/config/mod.rs`, absorbing `set_show_source` as its private helper. `config_show` collapses to ~25 lines, and the two conflict rules become unit-testable without a cwd.

**A second net.rs parallel, on the write side.** net routes every rule write through `open_rule_write` (src/main.rs:737–798) returning a `RuleWrite` struct (src/main.rs:693–712) — one admission, one place. config repeats the identical six-step preamble in three verbs: `config_set` (2594–2622), `config_list_edit` (2673–2703), `config_unset` (2742–2770), each doing `split_scope` → positional-count check → `config_cwd` → `resolve_key_target` → `trust::default_store_dir` → `admit_config_write`, then repeating the outcome-match/palette/println/`report_write_trust` tail (2626–2646, 2705–2731, 2772–2786). ~25 lines × 3 collapsible into one `open_key_write(verb, args, n_positionals) -> Result<KeyWrite, ExitCode>` in edit.rs, deliberately named to echo `open_rule_write`.

**Do NOT unify the two trust gates.** They look alike and are deliberately different, and both differences are documented. `scope_is_gated` (2440–2450) gates every scope except `Global`, including `Scope::File`; net's `open_rule_write` (src/main.rs:744–750) *refuses* `Scope::File` outright and gates only `Scope::Local`. `admit_config_write` (2452–2533) consults `crate::local_save_permitted` only when `--trust` was passed; `open_rule_write` (src/main.rs:762–772) consults it on every write. The reasons are written out at 2452–2470 and src/main.rs:590–612. A proposal to merge them would dissolve a real seam.

**`config_usage` is bypassed by the verb that most needs it.** `config_usage` (2367–2374) emits `diag::error("sbx: usage: {synopsis}")` then `ExitCode::from(2)`, and is used by all seven other verbs (15 call sites). `config_show`, defined 2200 lines earlier, open-codes the identical two statements four times: 76–80, 105–110, 135–140, 152–157. The text is byte-identical, so replacing each with `return config_usage("show");` (after the existing specific `diag::error`) is behaviour-preserving. This is the one-line justification for hoisting `config_usage` into `mod.rs` rather than leaving it in `edit.rs`.

**~600 lines of duplicated test fixtures.** `sample_config_view()` (3238–3349) is a 110-line `ConfigView` literal, and five tests already use the right pattern — build it, then mutate the two or three fields under test (3354, 3374, 3477, 3496, 3603). Six other tests instead re-inline the entire literal: 4184–~4300, 4327–~4425, 4493–~4560, 4584–~4685, 4719–~4820, 4854–~4970. Diffing 3240–3349 against 4327–4440 shows they differ in about eight fields (`env`, `binds`, `packages`, `mise`, the nixpkgs channel, `network`/`network_origin`, `apps`) and are byte-identical in the other ~60. Rewriting them as `let mut view = sample_config_view(); view.apps = vec![…]; view.network = NetworkView::Shared; view.network_origin = ProvenanceView::Default;` removes roughly 600 lines and takes `render.rs` from ~2760 to ~2160. Note `ConfigView` (src/config/view.rs:44) derives only `Serialize`, so a `..Default::default()` shorthand is not available without changing the view model — the mutate-the-fixture route needs no change to `src/config/view.rs` and is the one to take. This cleanup is worth doing *before* the split, since it shrinks the piece that stays largest.

**Guards that are not at risk.** `src/docs_coverage.rs` reads `docs-site/docs/guide` (its `guide()` helper, lines 24–26) and the help table; it never looks at source module paths, so the split cannot fail it. Completion (`src/cli/completion.rs`, `tests/completion.rs`) derives from `src/help.rs` pages and the CLI surface is unchanged. `tests/config.rs` (5481 lines) drives the binary, not the module, so it pins the behaviour through the whole refactor — take the split in one commit and run that file first.

splits.module_summary:
`src/sandbox/binds.rs` (4,612 lines) turns already-resolved host paths into a concrete `SandboxSpec` — the ordered mount plan, the cage environment, a synthetic identity, and the host-side runtime tree those mount sources live in. `fsmask.rs` (1,062) realises the `[fs]` deny/readonly table as decoy binds; `fhs.rs` (628) provisions the hermetic userland out of sbx's own store into a `Userland`.

The headline number is misleading. binds.rs is 1,706 lines of production code (of which 820 are comment lines and 86 blank — roughly 800 lines of actual code) followed by 2,906 lines of inline tests: `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` at 1707-3521 (1,815 lines, 57 tests) and `#[cfg(test)] mod smoke` at 3523-4612 (1,090 lines, 6 live-bwrap tests). 63% of the file is test code in two inline modules.

Internal sections of binds.rs, verified:
- 1-17 module header, including the integrity note ("the synthetic /etc must live outside every read-write bind").
- 23-132 in-cage FHS destination constants: `SANDBOX_HOME`(25), `SANDBOX_SHELL`(30), `LOADER_DEST`(36), `SANDBOX_BASH`(47), `SANDBOX_ENV`(55), `XDG_OPEN_INCAGE`(66), `OPEN_ROUTER_DIR`(95), `OPEN_ROUTER_INCAGE`(100), `SBX_INCAGE_DIR`(104), `OPT_DIR`(108), `CAGE_ZONEINFO`(112), `CAGE_LOCALTIME`(118), `DEFAULT_ZONE`(125), `SSH_CONFIG_INCAGE`(132).
- 135-340 the assembler's data types: `Userland`(145), `ExtraBind`(205), `NixMount`(224), `Overlay`(241), `ProjectRuntime`(265), `Identity`(281), `SandboxPaths`(287-340).
- 342-366 `assemble` — the pure keystone: `cage_mounts` + `cage_env` + `SandboxSpec::new`.
- 368-707 `cage_mounts` — the ordered mount plan, 340 lines, one function. This is the "everything the cage sees is declared in one place" property, and the doc at 355-366 states that bwrap argv order is the invariant.
- 709-743 `home_mountpoint_pins`.
- 745-859 `cage_env` — PATH construction and the structural environment.
- 861-901 `STRUCTURAL_DESTS`, kept in lockstep with `cage_mounts` by the test at 1845.
- 903-1000 nesting diagnostics: `Nesting`(904), `structural_nesting_conflict`(920), `structural_nesting_warning`(941).
- 1002-1081 mise/flake in-cage path vocabulary: `MISE_DATA_REL`(1006), `MISE_SHIMS_REL`(1014), `MISE_PROJECT_INCAGE`(1027), `mise_app_global_data_dir`(1036), `FLAKE_ROOTS_REL`(1044), `flake_roots_dir`(1048), `flake_out_link`(1055), `flake_out_link_hash`(1071), `flake_inline_incage`(1079).
- 1083-1105 `SHELL_RC_INCAGE`(1089) and `SHELL_RC_CONTENTS`(1101).
- 1107-1196 `mise_env`.
- 1198-1234 `CAGE_CA_BUNDLE`(1204), `cacert_env`(1211), `upsert_env`(1220), `join_paths`(1229).
- 1236-1306 synthetic file *contents*: `passwd_contents`(1238), `group_contents`(1249), `hosts_contents`(1268), `machine_id_contents`(1294).
- 1308-1413 host-side runtime keying: `Runtime`(1314), `project_runtime`(1328), `home_src`(1358), `project_id`(1369), `project_runtime_id`(1382), `project_identity`(1391), `canonicalize_project`(1404).
- 1415-1484 `current_identity`(1417), `materialize_etc`(1435), `write_atomic`(1476).
- 1486-1706 `build_spec` — the I/O orchestrator that stages every synthetic file and calls `assemble`.

fsmask.rs is 622 production lines forming one linear pipeline (`expand` 154 → `resolve_list` 235 / `admit` 305 → `guard_hard_links` 355 / `guard_git_tracked` 387 → `agent_binds` 503 / `task_mounts` 542), all sharing `Expanded`/`Masked`/`Decoys`. fhs.rs is 400 production lines: a locale sub-cluster (73-179) and one 220-line straight-line `resolve_userland` (181-400).
splits.rationale:
A split is worth doing, but the valuable part is not where the line count suggests, and I want to be explicit about that.

What must NOT move. `cage_mounts` (368-707) is 340 lines of one ordered list where "order is the invariant" (its own doc, 355-366: the `OPT_DIR` tmpfs at 386-389 is emitted before the config binds *precisely* so it shadows nothing, and every structural mount below depends on arriving after them). Splitting that function, or moving the in-cage destination constants (23-132) away from the mount that consumes them, would dissolve exactly the property the scope statement asks to preserve — a reader could no longer see the router's three-link mountpoint chain (`OPT_DIR` → `SBX_INCAGE_DIR` → `OPEN_ROUTER_DIR`) and the constants declaring it on one screen. `assemble`(342) → `cage_mounts` → `cage_env` and the five input types stay together. That is the module's cohesive core and it is genuinely one thing: ~700 lines, over half of it comment.

The real problem is that 2,906 of 4,612 lines are two inline `#[cfg(test)]` modules, and this repo already has the exact idiom for that: `src/sandbox/openpgp/mod.rs:437-438` and `src/sandbox/proxy/mod.rs:2058-2059` both declare `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;` against a sibling file (`proxy/tests.rs` is 10,357 lines). Extracting them costs zero visibility changes, zero doc-link rewrites, and zero risk to the security seam, and removes 63% of the file. That alone takes binds.rs from 4,612 to 1,706 and is where nearly all the value is.

Beyond that, three clusters are genuinely separable because they answer a different question than "what does the cage see":
- Host-side runtime keying (1308-1413 + the `ProjectRuntime`/`Identity` types) touches no in-cage constant in code at all — only in prose — yet it is the most externally consumed part of the module: `project_runtime_id` has 10 call sites across flake/prebuilt/nixhub/packages/task/launch, and `project_id`/`project_identity` are re-exported at `src/sandbox/mod.rs:127` and reached from `paths.rs`, `main.rs`, `cli/proc.rs`, `cli/net.rs`, `projects.rs`. It is why `binds` appears as a dependency of modules that have nothing to do with binds.
- The nesting diagnostic (903-1000) generates warning *prose* for config validation (`config/load.rs:183,261`); the launcher never calls it.
- The synthetic-file *content* producers (1091-1105, 1236-1306, 1427-1484) are pure byte generators plus two staging helpers, currently scattered across four disjoint ranges with `mise_env` and `cacert_env` interleaved between them.

Those three total ~370 lines and leave the core at ~1,350. That is a modest but real gain, and — critically — the moves are cheap: I grepped every `super::`/`crate::` path in all five moved ranges and found exactly one (`super::egress::TcpDestination` at line 1268). Everything else is self-contained.

I am recommending "worthwhile" rather than "strongly recommended" because the second step buys ~370 lines for three new files plus ~8 doc-link rewrites and ~12 visibility annotations, under a CLAUDE.md regime where each of those is a build-breaking mistake if botched. Do step 1 unconditionally; step 2 is a positive but smaller return.

fsmask.rs and fhs.rs should be left alone. fsmask is 622 production lines of one pipeline whose stages all share `Expanded`/`Masked`/`Decoys`; there is no seam that does not cut a data structure in half. fhs is 400 lines whose one large function is a straight-line list of `realise(...)` calls where the comments are the content.

proposed_modules.purpose: The unit-test module, moved out of the file it tests. Same idiom as src/sandbox/openpgp/tests.rs and src/sandbox/proxy/tests.rs. This is the single highest-value, lowest-risk step: it removes 1,815 lines from binds.rs without touching one line of production code.
proposed_modules.moves: The body of `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` — binds.rs lines 1709-3520 (the `mod tests {` header at 1707-1708 and its closing brace at 3521 are replaced by `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;` in binds/mod.rs). File opens with the existing header verbatim: `use super::*; use crate::testutil::TmpDir; use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;` (lines 1709-1711). All 57 tests and the 11 helpers (`userland` 1730, `nix_mount` 1764, `base_paths` 1775, `assembled` 1795, `assembled_from` 1801, `assembled_with_ssh_config` 1823, `assembled_with_every_conditional_mount` 1834, `assemble_with` 2443, `assemble_with_zone` 2453, `argv_strings` 2480, `env_strings` 2490, `ro` 2852, `rw` 2860) move unchanged.
proposed_modules.risk: Essentially none. `binds::tests` becomes a child module of `binds` instead of an inline one — identical name resolution, so `use super::*` still reaches every private item (`assemble`, `cage_mounts`, `SHELL_RC_CONTENTS`, `machine_id_contents`, `materialize_etc`, `project_runtime`, `canonicalize_project`). No visibility change, no doc link (the file has none; the one `[`assemble_with`]` reference at 2443 is inside the moved region and stays local). docs_coverage: `module_level_items()` skips files named `tests.rs` whole (src/docs_coverage.rs:996-998), so nothing new enters the guard. Requires converting binds.rs → binds/mod.rs, which forces the docs_coverage.rs:905 edit described under binds/synthetic.rs. Declare it as `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;` with NO `///` above the `mod` line — mise.toml:96-98 records that an outer doc comment on a `mod` declaration merges with the module header and shifts link resolution into the declaring module's scope.

proposed_modules.purpose: The six live-bwrap end-to-end tests, which are a different kind of test from the rest: they need real bwrap + userns + nix, skip rather than fail without them, and each runs a full launch. Named `smoke_tests.rs` (not `smoke.rs`) both to avoid confusion with the unrelated production module src/sandbox/smoke.rs and to hit the docs-coverage whole-file skip.
proposed_modules.moves: binds.rs lines 3523-4612: the module doc (3523-3528, rewritten from `///` to `//!` at the top of the new file), the header `use super::*; use crate::testutil::{TmpDir, fingerprint}; use std::process::Command;` (3531-3533), `prerequisites` (3537), and the six tests: `the_generated_argv_launches_a_working_hermetic_shell` (3547), `the_nix_ld_shim_serves_foreign_binaries_and_unskews_cross_channel_tools` (3658), `the_cage_runs_from_a_writable_per_project_store_seeded_with_the_base_closure` (3848), `the_cage_builds_a_fresh_derivation_offline_from_the_seeded_base` (4022), `network_reachable` (4209), `the_cage_self_equips_a_nix_tool_via_mise` (4233), `a_mise_used_tool_is_activated_on_path_in_a_later_launch` (4377), `a_global_app_cage_puts_both_mise_shims_dirs_on_path_and_splits_the_pool` (4522).
proposed_modules.risk: Two mechanical edits. (1) 21 path rewrites: the module reaches `super::super::argv` (7×), `super::super::fhs` (7×) and `super::super::projectstore` (4×); from `binds::smoke_tests` these gain one level. Rewrite them as `crate::sandbox::argv` / `crate::sandbox::fhs` / `crate::sandbox::projectstore` rather than adding a third `super`. (2) The module doc at 3525 says "The unit tests above check the argv *structure*" — "above" is false once the two live in sibling files; change to "the unit tests in `tests`". Otherwise no visibility change (it only uses `build_spec`, already `pub(crate)`). `skip_incapable!` still resolves: src/main.rs:13-15 declares `#[macro_use] mod testskip;` before every other module, so textual scope covers any module declared later, including this one. docs_coverage skips `*_tests.rs` whole.

proposed_modules.purpose: Where a project's host-side runtime state lives, and the identity it is keyed by — a different question from "what does the cage see", and the part of binds that the rest of the crate actually depends on. Zero references to any in-cage constant in code.
proposed_modules.moves: `ProjectRuntime` (261-275), `Runtime` (1308-1321), `project_runtime` (1323-1352), `home_src` (1354-1361), `project_id` (1363-1374), `project_runtime_id` (1376-1384), `project_identity` (1386-1395), `canonicalize_project` (1397-1413). Needs only `use std::io;` and `use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};` — I grepped 1308-1425 and 261-285 for `super::`/`crate::` and found none. `Identity` (277-285) and `current_identity` (1415-1425) deliberately do NOT come here; they exist only to feed passwd/group and go to synthetic.rs. `STRUCTURAL_DESTS` and every in-cage constant stay in mod.rs.
proposed_modules.risk:
Visibility: `project_runtime` and `canonicalize_project` are private today and must become `pub(super)` (visible throughout the `binds` subtree, so both binds/mod.rs's `build_spec` and binds/tests.rs reach them). `ProjectRuntime`, `Runtime`, `home_src`, `project_id`, `project_runtime_id`, `project_identity` are already `pub(crate)` and stay so — they must be, because binds/mod.rs re-exports them: `pub(crate) use self::runtime::{ProjectRuntime, Runtime, home_src, project_id, project_identity, project_runtime_id};`. That single line keeps every external path byte-identical: `binds::Runtime` (launch.rs, task.rs), `super::binds::project_runtime_id` (10 sites), and the crate-level re-export at src/sandbox/mod.rs:127 (`pub(crate) use binds::{DEFAULT_ZONE, project_id, project_identity, structural_nesting_warning};`) all keep working, and `super::super::binds::project_runtime_id` in the flake/prebuilt/nixhub tests too.
Rustdoc links that break and their fixes: line 1355 `[`build_spec`]` → `[`super::build_spec`]`; line 271 (`ProjectRuntime::mise_project_src`) `[`MISE_PROJECT_INCAGE`]` → `[`super::MISE_PROJECT_INCAGE`]` (resolves fine even though the const is private — a child module sees its parent's private items). Line 1324 `[`Runtime`]`, 1356 `[`project_runtime`]` and 1380 `[`canonicalize_project`]` become local and are unaffected. In binds/mod.rs the `//!` header at line 15 says "[`project_runtime`] places them in a sibling of the writable home" — that link now resolves only because of a re-export; either add `project_runtime` to a private `use self::runtime::{canonicalize_project, project_runtime};` in mod.rs (a private `use` binding is nameable from the parent module's own docs) or rewrite it as `[`runtime::project_runtime`]`. External doc links are safe: `[`super::binds::project_identity`]` (egress_stats.rs:28), `[`binds::Runtime`]` (launch.rs:1024, 5578) and `[`sandbox::project_id`]`/`[`sandbox::project_identity`]` (paths.rs:321,375; main.rs:529) all resolve through the re-exports.
Tests: `each_runtime_scope_keys_a_distinct_persistent_home` (3026-3060), `project_runtime_keys_the_per_project_mise_pool_per_project_and_app` (3286-3334) and `canonicalize_project_follows_symlinks_and_requires_a_directory` (3160-3178) may move into an inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` here, or stay in binds/tests.rs — `pub(super)` covers both. `synthetic_etc_lives_outside_the_writable_home` (3003-3024) must stay in binds/tests.rs; it drives `build_spec`.

proposed_modules.purpose: The bytes of the synthetic files the cage is handed read-only, and the two helpers that stage them. Today these seven items are scattered across four disjoint ranges (1091-1105, 1236-1306, 1427-1453, 1471-1484) with `mise_env`, `cacert_env`, `join_paths` and the whole runtime cluster interleaved; they belong together, and the module's own integrity note (lines 11-16) is about exactly this group.
proposed_modules.moves: `SHELL_RC_CONTENTS` (1091-1105), `passwd_contents` (1236-1246), `group_contents` (1248-1255), `hosts_contents` (1257-1282), `machine_id_contents` (1284-1306), `Identity` (277-285), `current_identity` (1415-1425), `materialize_etc` (1427-1453), `write_atomic` (1471-1484). proposed_modules.risk:

Deleting it is mandatory either way — the `stale` assertion at src/docs_coverage.rs:1082-1090 fails on an entry that no longer applies, and renaming binds.rs → binds/mod.rs alone already invalidates the path key.
Visibility: `hosts_contents` is `pub(super)` today (= visible in `sandbox`, called at task.rs:1057). In a submodule `pub(super)` would mean only `binds`, so it must become `pub(crate)` (or `pub(in crate::sandbox)`) and binds/mod.rs must carry `pub(super) use self::synthetic::hosts_contents;` — the re-export is legal only if the item is at least as visible as the `use`, hence `pub(crate)` rather than `pub(super)` on the item. `SHELL_RC_CONTENTS`, `passwd_contents`, `group_contents`, `machine_id_contents`, `current_identity`, `materialize_etc`, `write_atomic` go private → `pub(super)` (needed by `build_spec` in mod.rs and by binds/tests.rs). `Identity` stays `pub(crate)`; nothing outside `binds` names it, so mod.rs needs only a private `use self::synthetic::Identity;`.
Rustdoc: line 1431 `[`write_atomic`]` stays local. After the fix, build_spec's restored block links `[`assemble`]` and `[`SandboxSpec`]` from mod.rs, where both are in scope. No external doc link names any of these items.
Tests that move or stay: `the_shell_rc_sets_a_cage_naming_prompt_before_sourcing_bashrc` (1714-1728), `a_hosts_line_is_never_written_for_a_name_the_file_already_maps` (1881-1912), `the_synthetic_hosts_maps_localhost_and_the_cage_hostname` (1963-1985), `the_synthetic_machine_id_is_systemd_shaped_deterministic_and_per_home` (1987-2006), `synthetic_passwd_carries_the_identity_and_no_host_account` (3062-3077), `materialize_etc_writes_owner_only_files_with_the_synthetic_content` (3079-3096), `re_materializing_the_identity_installs_a_new_inode_instead_of_rewriting_in_place` (3098-3158) are all content-level and can move here; the `assemble_binds_a_read_only_*` tests must stay in binds/tests.rs since they assert mount output.
Cycles: `synthetic.rs` → `sandbox::egress` and → parent constants; `sandbox::egress` does not reach back into `binds::synthetic` (it uses `binds::project_identity` at egress.rs:769, which will live in runtime.rs). proposed_modules.purpose: The ergonomics tripwire that tells a user their `[[binds]]` entry nests with a structural mount and will not behave as written. A prose generator consumed only by config validation — the launcher never calls it, and it produces no mount.

Four files, 9,916 lines total (task.rs 4,436; task_control.rs 3,844; taskpool.rs 1,006; task_shim.rs 630). ~4,116 of those lines are inline `#[cfg(test)]` modules.

THE AXIS IS ALREADY RIGHT. The four files split along real trust seams: task.rs = the engine that derives a sibling cage from the agent cage and runs one invocation in it; task_control.rs = the two-socket plane (crossing + host-only) with its wire protocol and in-RAM record; task_shim.rs = the generated in-cage client that can express three verbs and nothing else; taskpool.rs = the host-side mise pool no cage mounts writable. splits.rationale:
The four-file axis is correct and should not be touched. What is wrong is depth inside two of the four, and the largest single cause is mechanical rather than architectural: 4,116 of 9,916 lines are inline `#[cfg(test)]` bodies. task.rs is 45% tests, task_control.rs is 55% tests. Moving those out-of-line costs literally nothing semantically — a child module declared `mod tests;` still sees every private item of its parent, the module path stays `sandbox::task::tests` so `cargo test --lib task::tests::…` filters are unchanged, `super::super::task_control::CAGE_TASK_UDS` (task.rs:3340) and `super::super::task_shim::write` (task_control.rs:2194) still resolve, and `src/docs_coverage.rs:997` skips files named `tests.rs`/`*_tests.rs` whole. The precedent is already in the tree: `src/sandbox/proxy/mod.rs:2058-2059` is exactly `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;` pointing at a 10,357-line `proxy/tests.rs`. That one move takes task.rs to ~2,420 and task_control.rs to ~1,740 — both then the size of `control/mod.rs` (2,410) and `proxy/mod.rs` (2,059), which nobody is asking to split.

Beyond that, three production clusters are worth extracting because each is a self-contained sub-problem with a single call site into it, not because of line count:

(1) The spawn-policy cluster (task.rs:1490-1779 + `lexical_join` 1782-1798). Eight methods that translate a declared `spawn`/`exec` list into a `ProcPolicy` keyed on absolute in-cage paths, reading the cage's mount list to resolve names, follow symlinks in cage space, and read `#!` lines. It is reached from exactly one place — `run_admitted` at task.rs:769 — and from nine tests. Its doc prose is the densest in the file and is about a subject (what a process *is* when the kernel enters it) that has nothing to do with mounts, credentials or capture.

(2) The cage-skeleton derivation (KEPT_DESTS 155-184, KEPT_ENV 186-205, `task_mounts` 2144-2174, `mount_dest` 2175-2188, `task_env` 2188-2199). This is one security allowlist and the filter that applies it, and the two halves currently sit 1,940 lines apart. The module header (task.rs:12-18) argues about precisely this pair; a reader following that argument has to jump twice.

(3) The in-RAM record in task_control.rs (189-560 + the two `LogEntry` constructors `finished` 936-956 and `refusal` 1149-1170, which sit 200 lines apart with identical "stamped by `TaskLog::push`" comments). It is a data structure with its own documented invariant ("the lock cannot be poisoned, and that is a property to keep", 428-441), its own wire encoding with a round-trip test, and its own sanitisation rules; it calls nothing back into the servers.

Honest counterweights, stated because they are real:
- `run_admitted` (685-950) is genuinely one 265-line sequence — credentials → needles → proc supervisor → proxy → build_spec → exec → redaction — where the ORDER is the security property (the proc shim must wrap innermost, the redaction must happen before anything is returned or logged). Do not split it. `build_spec` (990-1146) is likewise one ordered mount list where the ordering comments are the content. Both stay in mod.rs.
- The two servers `serve_cage` and `serve_host` should NOT be split into two files. The module's entire header is one argument about why these two exist as a pair; separating them separates the two halves of that argument, and they share `read_payloads`, `admit_quota`, `write_outcome`, `finished` and `refusal`.
- Splitting an inherent `impl TaskEngine` across files means "where is `TaskEngine::stop`" becomes a grep. task.rs already pays this (two impl blocks, 408 and 1316) and `proxy` pays it too (`ProxyCtx` has impls at ctx.rs:180 and ctx.rs:671). Mitigate with a two-line "the rest of TaskEngine lives in …" note in the mod.rs header, not by avoiding the split.
- taskpool.rs and task_shim.rs need nothing. Leave both.

`src/allowlist/` is the authorization surface for network egress: it turns declared config entries into typed match rules, and answers "is this request permitted?" on three planes (inspected-over-TLS, inspected-cleartext, raw L4 splice). It is consumed by the config layer (classify + display + warnings), the filtering proxy (live verdicts), and `sbx test net`.

`src/allowlist/grammar.rs` (574 lines) is ALREADY the parse seam and needs no change. Its own header says so: "Turns text into the matcher's data model; the matching itself lives in [`super`]." It holds `Slot` (12-33), `classify` (41), `classify_in` (53), `split_scheme` (111), `split_method_prefix` (137), `parse_methods` (165), `parse_default_methods` (192), `classify_kind` (217), `reject_catch_all` (259), `scheme_of` (295), `has_explicit_port` (310), `split_host_ports` (328), `parse_ports` (362), `parse_port` (395), `parse_url_target` (414), `parse_tcp_target` (471), `parse_path_rule` (530), `is_valid_hostname` (561). It carries no `#[cfg(test)]` block — all of its tests live in mod.rs.

`src/allowlist/mod.rs` (4089 lines) is 57% tests. Its internal sections, verified by line:
- 1-80: module header doc (the rule-syntax reference; the only intra-doc links are `[`regex`]` at 66 and `[`Request::canonical_url`]` at 72).

- 441-560 THE MATCH PREDICATES: `impl Rule { concrete_host 447, matches 459, matches_deny 465, matches_mute 475, opens_every_host 493 }` (441-505); `impl RuleKind { matches 513, matches_any_port 542 }` (507-560).

The layering is already acyclic: canon ← rule ← matching ← policy, with grammar hanging off rule+canon.
splits.rationale:
Worthwhile, but the reason is not the 4089 lines — it is that 2348 of them are tests and the parse seam the task asks about is already cut. Extracting `mod tests` alone takes mod.rs to ~1745 lines with literally zero visibility, doc-link or guard changes, following a convention the repo already uses twice (`src/config/mod.rs:5841`, `src/sandbox/proxy/mod.rs:2059` both declare `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;` against an external file). That is the whole first stage and it is nearly free.

The remaining ~1740 lines then split along three seams the code itself already draws:

1. `canon.rs` (562-680) is a true leaf: seven pure string/segment functions with no dependency on `Rule`, `EgressPolicy`, or anything else in the module. `canonical_host`'s own doc names the property — "Applied on both sides — the rule (`parse_url_target`) and the request (`Request::new`)" — and `apex_or_subdomain`'s says "One definition for the three places that ask it". These are shared by parse, match, render and the http2 host list. Putting them in one leaf file makes the anti-evasion normal form auditable in isolation.

2. `matching.rs` (371-439, 453-560, 1709-1719) is the security keystone the module header spends 40 lines on: `Request` canonicalized once, then the rule-level predicates. ~200 lines that answer exactly one question. Separating it from the data model means `impl Rule` lives in two files and `impl RuleKind` in two — a real, acknowledged cost — but `Rule`'s shape is 30 lines and its behaviour is the part anyone audits.

3. `policy.rs` (775-1707) is the largest new file at ~930 lines and is genuinely one thing: a policy value plus the three-plane verdict. `explain`, `explain_clear` and `l4_decision` are deliberately co-designed (each doc cross-references the other two on deny-wins and opt-in asymmetry) and must NOT be separated from each other; this proposal keeps them together.

What I am NOT proposing, and why: (a) render/serialize IS separable — `Display for Rule`, `RuleKind::render`, `Display for RuleKind`, `Methods::prefix`, `Ports::render_suffix`, `display_host` form a closed cluster and are the exact inverse of `classify` — but it totals ~100 lines and extracting it fragments `impl Ports` and `impl Methods` across two files each, for a type with three methods. Keep it as a contiguous, labelled section at the bottom of `rule.rs` instead. (b) Splitting the `EgressPolicy` inherent impl at 1370/1371 is tempting and defensible but is a second-order move; see other_observations. (c) `grammar.rs` should be left exactly as it is.
