splits.other_observations:
1. A REAL DEFECT THE SPLIT WOULD SURFACE AND FIX. `EgressPolicy`'s type doc has been severed from its type. mod.rs:829-836 ("A classified egress policy: an allow list, a deny list, and a default action…") is the first paragraph of the doc block that now sits on `Http2Host` (struct at line 850) — `Http2Host`'s own prose starts mid-block at line 837 ("A `[network] http2` entry: …"). `EgressPolicy` itself, at line 955, has no doc comment at all: line 954 is a bare `#[derive]` preceded by the end of `DEFAULT_BODY_MAX` at 952. This is exactly the failure mode `every_module_level_item_carries_a_doc_comment` was written for (`src/docs_coverage.rs:1042-1055` describes it verbatim), and it is currently papered over by the grandfather entry at docs_coverage.rs:857. The fix is a clean cut at 836/837: move 829-836 down to sit above line 954, and delete the entry from `UNDOCUMENTED_MODULE_ITEMS`. Worth doing whether or not the split happens.

2. mod.rs's `use` lines are load-bearing for grammar.rs and will break silently. `grammar.rs` has exactly one import — `use super::*;` at line 6 — yet it uses `IpAddr` (grammar.rs:231, 235, 342, 458, 486, 546) and `Regex::new` (grammar.rs:57). Those names reach it through mod.rs:83 (`use std::net::IpAddr;`) and mod.rs:85 (`use regex::Regex;`), which are private `use` bindings glob-imported by the child. Once mod.rs's code moves out, mod.rs itself no longer references `fmt`, `IpAddr` or `Regex`, and `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` will reject them as unused. Add `use std::net::IpAddr;` and `use regex::Regex;` to grammar.rs (and to rule.rs/matching.rs/policy.rs as each needs them, plus `use std::fmt;` in rule.rs for the `Display` impls), and delete mod.rs:82-85.

3. Use explicit re-export lists, not globs, for the new modules. mod.rs should end up as: the 1-80 header, then `mod canon; mod grammar; mod matching; mod policy; mod rule; #[cfg(test)] mod tests;`, then `pub(crate) use grammar::*;` (unchanged — it is the existing contract, and 51 call sites reach `allowlist::classify` through it) plus explicit lists for the rest: `pub(crate) use canon::{canonical_host, canonical_segments};`, `pub(crate) use matching::{Request, rule_matches};`, `pub(crate) use policy::{DEFAULT_BODY_MAX, DEFAULT_DNS_CACHE_TTL, DEFAULT_IDLE_TIMEOUT, DEFAULT_MAX_CONNECTIONS, Decision, DefaultAction, EgressPolicy, Http2Host, L4Decision, WebsocketSecret};`, `pub(crate) use rule::{Layer, Methods, Ports, Rule, RuleKind, host_port_rule};`. Five globs feeding five `use super::*;` children is the one way this split can bite: two modules exporting the same identifier becomes an E0659 ambiguity at the use site. Explicit lists also make the module's crate-facing surface readable in one screen. All 25 distinct `allowlist::X` paths used elsewhere in the crate are covered by that list — I enumerated them.

4. There is no cyclic-dependency risk at the language level (Rust permits mutual references between sibling modules in a crate), and the intended layering is acyclic anyway: canon ← {rule, grammar} ← matching ← policy. Worth writing into each new file's header so it does not decay.

5. A SECOND-ORDER SPLIT I AM NOT RECOMMENDING YET, but which is real: `impl EgressPolicy` (1028-1656) cleanly divides at line 1370/1371. The settings half (1029-1370, ~340 lines) is `new`, `with_rules`, `settings_dropped_from`, and 30 builder/accessor pairs whose docs say over and over "never a verdict" — `pool` (1249), `ca_roots` (1300), `capture_level` (1318), `http2_hosts` (1348), `speaks_http2` (1356). The verdict half (1372-1655, ~285 lines) is the security-relevant code. If the dilution ever becomes a problem, the mechanical move is `src/allowlist/policy/verdict.rs` as a CHILD of `policy` (not a sibling), which needs zero visibility changes at all: a descendant module sees its ancestor's private fields, so `muted`/`explain`/`explain_clear`/`l4_decision`/`method_denied`/`method_denied_clear`/`splices_any`/`apply_default_methods`/`l4_l7_conflicts` can read `self.allow`/`self.deny`/`self.mute`/`self.default_action` unchanged. I would not do it in the same pass as the primary split.

6. `permits` (mod.rs:1407, with `#[allow(dead_code)]` at 1406) is genuinely test-only, but across three test modules — 87 call sites in allowlist's own tests, plus src/sandbox/proxy/tests.rs:6752-6826 and src/config/tests.rs:6938-6945 — so it must stay `pub(crate)`. `#[cfg(test)]` would be more honest than `#[allow(dead_code)]` and would let the allowance go; it compiles for all three consumers. Minor, orthogonal to the split.

7. RENDER, THE AXIS THE TASK ASKS ABOUT, IN FULL. The cluster is `Display for Rule` (721-741), `RuleKind::render` (743-767), `Display for RuleKind` (769-773), `Methods::prefix` (280-286), `Ports::render_suffix` (348-368), `display_host` (675-680), `Http2Host::display` (890-902) — about 100 lines, closed (nothing else calls `prefix`, `render`, or `render_suffix`), and the exact inverse of `classify`, a contract two tests pin (`display_round_trips_each_kind` at 3423, `a_method_prefix_round_trips_through_display` at 3523). It is separable. I am still not proposing a file for it: extracting it fragments `impl Ports` (3 remaining methods) and `impl Methods` (2 remaining) across two files each, and pulls `Http2Host::display` away from `Http2Host::parse`, for a file smaller than the module header. Keep it as the final, section-commented block of rule.rs, with the header naming grammar.rs as its inverse. If a later change makes rendering non-trivial — a machine-readable serialization beside the human one, say — revisit it then.

splits.module_summary:
Two modules, both of which are "one table, read many ways" — but they are not the same shape internally.

**src/help.rs (3,850 lines)** is the CLI's single source of truth for usage text. It is ~79% flat data.
- 1–23: module doc (the WHY: one table, aliases resolved-but-never-offered, the deliberate seam that option prose duplicates each handler's parser).
- 25–29: `use` (std + `crate::style::Palette`).
- 31–44: the two types — `type Opt` (31–32), `struct Page` (34–44), both private, 5 private fields.
- 46–3089: `const PAGES: &[Page]` — 104 page literals, 3,035 lines. Verified group sizes: net 18 pages/653 lines, config 9/330, task 9/281, app 9/273, proc 10/268, plugins (incl. `plugins store`) 17/257, run 1/142, session 5/106, storage 1/98, projects 2/75, bundle 3/68, upgrade 1/65, fs 2/57, logs 1/51, gc 1/50, ssh-agent 2/45, plus 12 smaller namespaces. Five `// ---- … ----` banner comments (48, 1912, 2108, 2134, 2840, 2951) try to group it and have already drifted (`bundle` at 2173 sits under "net subcommands"; `projects show` at 2049 under "app subcommands"; most subcommand pages sit under "top-level commands").
- 3091–3125: `const ALIASES` — 20 alternate spellings.
- 3127–3197: the query layer — `canonical` (3127), `find` (3135), `children` (3141), `synopsis_of` (3153), `synopsis` (3158), `is_command` (3165), `is_command_path` (3171), `subcommands_of` (3178), `all_paths` (3188, `#[cfg(test)]`), `options_of` (3195).
- 3199–3337: the renderer, which touches no path logic at all — `item` (3200), `paint_synopsis` (3213), `paint_inline_code` (3241), `top_level` (3248), `render` (3278).
- 3339–3433: the entry points — `show` (3341), `resolve_path` (3364), `maybe_help` (3390), `dispatch` (3402), `top_level_usage` (3423), `page_usage` (3431).
- 3435–3850: `mod tests` — 12 tests plus 5 helpers, including `dispatched_alias_pairs` (3727–3792) and `DISPATCHERS` (3679–3691), a source-text scanner that reads `src/cli/*.rs` to prove every dispatched alias is declared in `ALIASES`.

Call graph: `find`/`children` read `PAGES`; everything public reads `find`/`children`; `render`/`top_level` read `Page` fields + `children` + `PAGES` and nothing else. The renderer is a leaf; the table is a leaf; nothing in the table knows the renderer exists.

**src/cli/completion.rs (1,851 lines)** is the completion oracle — ~40% tests, ~60% a genuinely coupled pipeline (words → command path → operand slot → `ValueKind` → candidates).
- 1–33: module doc + `use` (`crate::{config, diag, help, plugins, session}`, `plugins::stores`, `sandbox::proc_control`).
- 35–46: `SHELLS` (35–36), `DESC_WIDTH` (38–41), `FILES` (43–46).
- 48–75 / 77–108: `completion_cmd`, `complete_cmd` (the `__complete` protocol).
- 110–145: `insertable` — the shell-injection gate every candidate crosses, with a 20-line rationale.
- 139–234: `candidates` — the dispatcher of the whole file.
- 236–252: `flag_menu`.
- 254–540 ("Values." banner at 254): `ValueKind` (258–290), `RuleList` (292–297), `removal_list` (299–314), `rule_values` (316–330), `rule_files` (332–346), `value_candidates` (348–365), `registry_values` (367–498), `config_tokens` (500–519), `config_files` (521–527), `project_config_file` (529–534), `global_config_file` (536–540). This is the only I/O in the file, and it runs on a keystroke.
- 542–719 ("operand grammar" banner): `Operand` (546–557), `all_literal_words` (559–575), `operand_slots` (577–618), `metavar_of` (620–639), `optional_of` (641–655), `is_literal` (657–670), `kind_of_metavar` (672–712), `is_pending_page` (714–719).
- 721–825 ("cursor" banner): `PendingWord` (725–734), `cursor_value_kind` (736–825).
- 827–971 ("value of a flag" banner): `flag_value_kind` (831–867), `alternation_cells` (869–898), `flag_takes_value` (895–905), `flag_metavar_kind` (906–925), `flag_literals` (927–942), `flag_tail` (944–971).
- 973–1017 ("Flags." banner): `flag_names` (977–995), `describe` (997–1017).
- 1019–1097: the `BASH` and `ZSH` script constants.
- 1099–1851: `mod tests` — 4 word-list helpers plus 24 tests, several of which sweep `help::all_paths()` over the whole table.

Dependency direction is already strictly layered and acyclic: grammar (`operand_slots`, `metavar_of`, `flag_*`) → value types (`ValueKind`, `removal_list`); the registry readers (`registry_values`, `rule_values`, `config_tokens`) call nothing in the grammar half.
splits.rationale:
The verdict is strong for **help.rs** and merely worthwhile for **completion.rs**; they are different cases.

help.rs is not one cohesive anything — it is a 3,035-line catalogue, a 139-line renderer that never touches path logic, a 71-line query layer, and a 416-line guard suite that mostly reads *other files' source text*. The engine a reader needs in order to understand how help works starts at line 3127, i.e. after 81% of the file. Nothing about the split touches the property the module doc actually guarantees: "one table is the single source of truth" is about there being exactly one `PAGES` slice with exactly one aggregation point, not about which file the literal sits in. Moving the const verbatim into `src/help/pages.rs` preserves that literally — one const, one definition site.

The cost is unusually low, and this is the load-bearing reason for the strong verdict: in Rust a child module can see its parent's *private* items **and their private fields**, so `src/help/pages.rs` can construct all 104 `Page { … }` literals with `Page`, `Opt` and every field left exactly as private as they are today. The only visibility change the whole help split needs is `pub(super)` on `PAGES` plus four items in the new `render.rs`. Exactly one intra-doc link in the crate is affected (`src/help.rs:3092`). The four links in the module header (`[\`Page\`]`, `[\`synopsis\`]`, `[\`maybe_help\`]`, `[\`ALIASES\`]` at lines 3, 6, 9, 15) and the two external ones (`src/cli/session.rs:16`, `src/docs_coverage.rs:638`) all name items that stay in `mod.rs` and are untouched. And the const sits at module level in both the old and new file, so rustfmt reproduces it byte-for-byte.

completion.rs is the weaker case and I want to be honest about it: 1,851 lines minus 753 lines of tests is a ~1,100-line body that really is one pipeline, and I am explicitly **not** proposing to fragment that pipeline. `candidates` → `cursor_value_kind` → `operand_slots`/`flag_value_kind` is a chain that reads best in one place, and `insertable` must stay welded to `complete_cmd` because its whole argument (lines 110–129) is that it is the *single* point every candidate crosses — moving it next to a producer would dissolve that seam. What I do propose is three cuts that follow seams the file already draws with banner comments and that the module doc already argues for: the 753-line test module out (matching `src/config/tests.rs`), the ~283-line registry-reading half out (the only I/O, the only part that touches the store layout, the session registry, the plugin registry and the proc control plane on a keystroke — worth being a file you can point at), and the two 40-line shell-script string constants out. The remaining `grammar.rs` cut is the one genuine cohesion win: it collects every function whose job is "parse a human-written option row from the help table", which is the code most likely to be edited when a page's grammar changes, and putting `kind_of_metavar` and `flag_metavar_kind` in one file exposes a near-duplicate table that is currently 240 lines apart.

What I am not recommending: sharding `PAGES` further by namespace. It is a real but modest win and it introduces the one new failure mode this design does not have today (a page group nobody aggregates). Design and guard are in other_observations if it is wanted later.

proposed_modules.purpose: Hold the page catalogue and nothing else, so that src/help/mod.rs is the ~250-line help engine rather than a 3,850-line file whose logic starts at line 3127.
proposed_modules.moves: `const PAGES: &[Page]` verbatim — its doc comment at src/help.rs:46 through the closing `];` at src/help.rs:3089 (104 `Page { … }` literals, 3,035 lines), including the five `// ---- … ----` banner comments at 48, 1912, 2108, 2134, 2840, 2951. New file header: `use super::{Opt, Page};` and the declaration becomes `pub(super) const PAGES: &[Page]`. STAYS in src/help/mod.rs: `type Opt` (31–32) and `struct Page` (34–44) with all five fields left private, `const ALIASES` (3091–3125), and the whole query layer `canonical`/`find`/`children`/`synopsis_of`/`synopsis`/`is_command`/`is_command_path`/`subcommands_of`/`all_paths`/`options_of` (3127–3197).
proposed_modules.risk: Visibility: exactly one change — `PAGES` gains `pub(super)`. `Page` and `Opt` and every one of `Page`'s five fields stay private: a child module sees its parent's private items and private fields, so all 104 struct literals compile unchanged. Intra-doc: one link breaks — src/help.rs:3092, the `ALIASES` doc, says "Aliases stay out of [`PAGES`]"; mod.rs will carry `use pages::PAGES;` (needed by `find` at 3137 and `children` at 3143 anyway), which makes the bare link resolve again, but if that import is elided the link must be written `[`pages::PAGES`]` or `mise run rustdoc` fails. Nothing else: the module-header links at src/help.rs:3, 6, 9, 15 name `Page`/`synopsis`/`maybe_help`/`ALIASES`, all of which stay in mod.rs; src/cli/session.rs:16 and src/docs_coverage.rs:638 name `help::maybe_help` / `crate::help::subcommands_of`, both unmoved. Tests: `every_page_renders_balanced_in_color` (3496) and `top_level_commands_are_listed_alphabetically` (3826) iterate `PAGES` and go to src/help/tests.rs with an explicit `use super::pages::PAGES;`. Cycles: none — pages.rs imports only `super::{Opt, Page}` and is a pure leaf. docs-coverage: `module_level_items` (src/docs_coverage.rs:966) matches only column-0 `fn|struct|enum|trait|union`, so a bare `const` triggers no new doc requirement; document it anyway (it already has a doc comment to carry across). rustfmt: the const is at module level in both files, so the move is byte-identical and `cargo fmt --check` stays green. Real hazard: a botched copy silently drops a page — but `every_cli_verb_has_a_reference_page` (src/docs_coverage.rs:79), the alias tests, and tests/help.rs (which resolves every accepted path to a page) all fail loudly if one goes missing.

proposed_modules.purpose: Isolate the presentation layer — ANSI painting and page layout — which reads Page fields and `children` and knows nothing about aliases, path resolution or dispatch.
proposed_modules.moves: src/help.rs:3199–3337 verbatim: `item` (3200), `paint_synopsis` (3213), `paint_inline_code` (3241), `top_level` (3248), `render` (3278). New file header: `use super::pages::PAGES;`, `use super::{Page, children};`, `use crate::style::Palette;`. STAYS in mod.rs: `show` (3341), `resolve_path` (3364), `maybe_help` (3390), `dispatch` (3402), `top_level_usage` (3423), `page_usage` (3431) — the entry points that decide *which* page and *which* stream's palette, calling `render::render` / `render::top_level`.
proposed_modules.risk: Visibility: four items gain `pub(super)` — `render` and `top_level` (called from `show`, `page_usage`, `dispatch`, `top_level_usage` in mod.rs), plus `paint_synopsis` and `paint_inline_code` (called directly by the tests at src/help.rs:3504 and 3526). `item` stays private to render.rs. `children` (3141) and `Page` stay private in mod.rs and remain visible to `help::render` as a descendant module — no change there. splits.other_observations:
**A hard prerequisite for the completion split, easy to miss.** src/docs_coverage.rs:861 contains the literal `("cli/completion.rs", "completion_cmd")` inside `UNDOCUMENTED_MODULE_ITEMS` (declared at :856). The moment `src/cli/completion.rs` becomes `src/cli/completion/mod.rs`, that key stops matching, and `every_module_level_item_carries_a_doc_comment` (:1058) fails on its *stale* assertion at :1082–1092 ("names items that are now documented or gone"). Do not retarget the key — write the missing `///` on `completion_cmd` (src/cli/completion.rs:48, currently the only undocumented item in either file) and delete the entry. The list's own doc at :830–834 says it can only shrink. Nothing equivalent exists for help.rs: it has no entry in that table, so the help split has no docs-coverage prerequisite at all.

**A coverage hole the completion split opens, worth writing down.** `dispatched_alias_pairs` (src/help.rs:3727) does a non-recursive `read_dir` of `src/cli` filtered to `extension == "rs"`. After the move, `src/cli/completion/*.rs` is outside its scan. That is harmless today — I verified by re-implementing the scan that every `Some(...) =>` arm carrying two or more subcommand spellings lives in app.rs:35, fs.rs:18, net.rs:52, plugins.rs:26 and :761, proc.rs:28 and :30, projects.rs:20 and :22, secret.rs:26, session.rs:24 and :29, sshagent.rs:17, task.rs:40 and :47 (fifteen pairs; completion.rs contributes none), so the `pairs.len() >= 19` floor at src/help.rs:3802 is unaffected. But the scan is now structurally blind to any future dispatcher placed in a `src/cli/<name>/` directory, and `DISPATCHERS` (src/help.rs:3679) keys on bare file names like `"mod.rs"`, which would collide across directories if the walk were ever made recursive. Either make `walk` recursive and key `DISPATCHERS` on the path relative to `src/cli`, or leave a comment at :3727 saying the scan is top-level-only by design.

**A genuine near-duplicate that the grammar.rs cut would put side by side.** `kind_of_metavar` (src/cli/completion.rs:694–706) and `flag_metavar_kind` (:911–923) are two name→`ValueKind` tables 200 lines apart. They agree exactly on `"id"|"pid"|"session" => Sessions`, `"name"|"app"|"profile"|"sketch" => Apps`, `"store" => Stores`, `"key" => ConfigKeys`, and differ only at the edges: the operand table adds `"scheme"` to Plugins, `"invocation"` to Tasks and `"out"` to Files; the flag table adds `"locator"`, `"location"`, `"key-file"` and `"dir:"` to Files. A metavariable name added to one and not the other silently stops completing on the other side, and neither `every_value_position_is_completed_or_declared_unenumerable` (:1714) nor `every_documented_flag_completes_on_the_page_that_documents_it` (:1565) would catch it, because each sweeps only its own half. The mechanical fix once both live in grammar.rs: a `fn shared_metavar_kind(name: &str) -> Option<ValueKind>` holding the four agreed rows plus the common Files set, with each caller keeping only its own extra arms and its own guards (`flag_metavar_kind`'s uppercase/`=` rejection, `kind_of_metavar`'s `plugins`/`projects`/`rule`/pending page overrides). That is ~20 lines collapsed and one drift class removed. I would do this *after* the move, not during it, so the move stays a pure relocation.

**The PAGES banner comments have already drifted, which is the argument for the optional second step.** src/help.rs:48 says "top-level commands" but the block runs to 1911 and contains most of the `proc`, `fs`, `secret`, `task`, `session` and `config` subcommand pages; src/help.rs:2134 says "net subcommands" but `bundle` (2173), `bundle export` (2197) and `bundle import` (2212) are top-level commands sitting inside it; src/help.rs:1912 says "app subcommands" but `projects show` (2049) is in it. If a namespace shard is ever wanted, the concrete design is: `src/help/pages/` holding `net.rs` (18 pages / 653 lines), `config.rs` (9/330), `task.rs` (9/281), `app.rs` (9/273), `proc.rs` (10/268), `plugins.rs` (17/257, `plugins store` included), `session.rs` (5/106), and `misc.rs` for the remaining ~28 pages, each exposing `pub(super) const PAGES: &[Page]`, with `src/help/pages/mod.rs` holding `const GROUPS: &[&[Page]]` and `pub(super) fn pages() -> impl Iterator<Item = &'static Page>`. The five call sites that read `PAGES` today (src/help.rs:3137 `find`, :3143 `children`, :3189 `all_paths`, :3258 `top_level`, and the tests at :3499 and :3848) become `pages()`. The cost is the one new failure mode the flat version does not have — a group file nobody lists in `GROUPS` — so it must ship with a guard in the house style of `module_level_items`: `read_dir("src/help/pages")` and assert the count of `.rs` files (minus `mod.rs`) equals `GROUPS.len()`. My recommendation is to skip this: `pages.rs` is a catalogue you navigate by grepping `path: &["net", "logs"]`, the localized-diff benefit is modest, and the aggregation seam is the only part of this whole proposal that can lose a page silently.

**Two smaller notes.** `paint_inline_code` (src/help.rs:3241–3246) is a one-line forward to `crate::style::paint_spans`; it earns its place only because its doc comment records the non-terminal-is-plain invariant, so keep it (and its doc) rather than inlining the call at its four use sites. And `all_paths` (src/help.rs:3188) is a `#[cfg(test)] pub fn` consumed by *another module's* tests (src/cli/completion.rs:1527, 1567, 1640, 1720, 1764) — an unusual but deliberate cross-module test API; it stays in `src/help/mod.rs` under the proposal, so those five call sites need no change.

**Direct answer to the shape question: the authorization *verdict* is stated once; the machinery on either side of it is stated two to four times, and the codebase's own comments record three bugs that came from exactly that.**

Stated once, and correctly so: the policy verdict `decide_https` (mod.rs:664, called from tunnel.rs:231, forward.rs:92, h2mitm.rs:271); DNS + SSRF `resolve_checked`; framing `inspect_framing` (wire.rs:135); needle matching `carries_secret` (mod.rs:1305); injection matching `matching_injection_ids` (mod.rs:1215); signer refusal prose `signer_refusal_message` (mod.rs:1284); refusal body `refusal_body` (mod.rs:1673); header-strip rule `header_name_eq` (wire.rs:20); masking bytes `redact_in_place` (mod.rs:1659).

Restated, with line cites:
1. **WS-into-injected-host refusal** — tunnel.rs:253-276 ≡ forward.rs:108-130. Verbatim but for the writer.
2. **Injection + signer + body-hold + budget block** — tunnel.rs:307-474 ≈ forward.rs:158-307. I diffed these: ~165 lines each, differing only in identifier names (`connect_host/imethod/itarget` vs `host/method/path`), the refusal writer (`respond_refusal_tls` vs `write_refusal`), the reader (`&mut br` vs a scoped `BufReader::new(&client)`), and one extra `&& !ws_upgrade` (tunnel.rs:355). h2mitm.rs:356-417 is a genuinely different third statement (no held body on h2).
3. **Pool eligibility** — tunnel.rs:481-491 ≡ forward.rs:312-315.
4. **Upstream take + one-shot replay loop** — tunnel.rs:496-540 + 668-733 ≈ forward.rs:320-330 + 432-478.
5. **`masks_reflection`** — the identical three-line predicate at tunnel.rs:784-788, forward.rs:520-524, h2mitm.rs:580-584.
6. **401 → `credential_refused`** — tunnel.rs:858-859 ≡ forward.rs:576-577 ≡ h2mitm.rs:557-558.
7. **`observe_head` placement** — tunnel.rs:472-474, forward.rs:305-307, cleartext.rs:159, h2mitm.rs:415-416.
8. **Response relay tail** (`relay_response_head` → empty-head `upstream-closed` → `set_status` → framed pump → park) — tunnel.rs:795-899 ≈ forward.rs:515-607 ≈ cleartext.rs:267-295.
9. **Allow record + flow + capture open** — tunnel.rs:520-552, forward.rs:332-352, h2mitm.rs:432-465.

The comments themselves name three defects this produced: forward.rs:83-89 (the absolute form judged a WS upgrade as its literal `GET`, which a `CONNECT` to the same host refused); h2mitm.rs:552-556 (only the h2 plane failed to refresh on a 401, so a stale token stayed stale on that plane alone); websocket.rs:786-789 (`proxy-authorization` forwarded to the origin on the upgrade and h2 rebuilds only). Each is a decision that was written out N times and drifted at one of them — which is precisely the failure mode mod.rs:22-25 says the design exists to prevent. The design is right; the two HTTP/1.1 planes just never finished obeying it.

**Why "worthwhile" and not "strongly recommended".** The two biggest files each have a real defence. `mod.rs` at 2,059 lines is a *deliberately* central vocabulary, and scattering it across six files makes the vocabulary harder to read whole — but 8 disjoint clusters with clean edges is more than one file should carry, and 165 of its lines (`Head`, the head readers, `parse_status_code`, `reserialize_request`) are plain HTTP/1.1 wire concerns that `wire.rs` currently reaches back *up* for through `use super::*`. `tunnel.rs` is one 875-line function, and I am **not** proposing to carve it up: it is a linear sequence whose whole value is that a reader can follow one request from head to close, and chopping it into `step_5`/`step_7` helpers would destroy that. What I propose is narrower — lift out only the ~200 lines it shares verbatim with `forward.rs`, so the sequence stays visible and the shared decisions stop being copies.

**The cost is unusually low here**, and I verified the mechanism rather than assuming it: `tests.rs`, `tunnel.rs`, `forward.rs`, `cleartext.rs`, `websocket.rs` and `wire.rs` all begin with `use super::*;`, and mod.rs already re-globs its children (`use wire::*;` at mod.rs:214, `use websocket::*;` at :213). So a new child module plus one `use newmod::*;` line in mod.rs leaves every sibling and all 10,357 lines of `tests.rs` compiling with **zero edits**. Intra-doc links survive the same chain, and I can prove it from this tree rather than from memory: mod.rs:104 links ``[`inspect_framing`]`` and ``[`head_carries_control_byte`]``, both `pub(super) fn` defined in wire.rs and reachable only through that glob, under a build that denies rustdoc warnings. `docs_coverage.rs` is unaffected — it checks CLI verbs, config fields and profiles, plus a (file, symbol) allowlist at docs_coverage.rs:856-943 whose only entry in this directory is `("sandbox/proxy/websocket.rs", "relay_websocket")` (docs_coverage.rs:935), and `relay_websocket` does not move under this proposal.

Do modules 1-3 (the deduplication and the two obvious mis-filings). Modules 4-7 are honest tidying of mod.rs with modest payoff — worth doing in the same pass, not worth a pass of their own. Module 8 is optional.

proposed_modules.purpose: The headline. What the two inspected HTTP/1.1 planes do BETWEEN the verdict and the wire, stated once instead of twice — closing the ~200 lines that tunnel.rs and forward.rs currently keep as near-verbatim copies of each other. This adds to mod.rs's stated "shared vocabulary" rather than merging the planes: each plane keeps its own sequencing and its own refusal writer, and only the decisions become shared. New module doc explains that this is the tunnel/forward common denominator and that h2 states its own (no held body, no CONNECT).

**The highest-risk item in this proposal, and the only one that changes control flow on the security path.** Every refusal it absorbs is a fail-closed exit whose `ctx.outcome(...)`/`ctx.push_log(...)` call must fire exactly once — mod.rs:1968-1983 records that the push_log/outcome split is "the part most likely to drift under copying", and this moves ~10 such sites. Do it with the existing tests green at every step and lift one block at a time (`refuse_ws_into_injected_host` first — it is 23 lines and self-contained — then `masks_reflection` and `note_final_status`, then `prepare_credentials` last).

Both resolve today via h2mitm's explicit import, so updating that import fixes both. mod.rs:1235 mentions `observe_head` in prose (not a link). No `[`matching_injection_ids`]`, `[`injected_names`]`, `[`any_refreshable`]` or `[`signer_refusal_message`]` links exist anywhere.

Tests: no `#[cfg(test)]` block moves — `tests.rs` reaches these through `use super::*` and only touches `reserialize_request` (1 site) among them. The plane-level tests that cover these paths live in `tests.rs` and `forward.rs`'s `mod tests` (forward.rs:614-714, which asserts the `ws-injection-refused` transcript at forward.rs:706) and are unaffected.

The one thing to watch: `hold_request_body` on the tunneled plane reads from the persistent `BufReader` that carries pipelined requests; forward.rs:237-238 deliberately scopes its reader because over-reading is harmless there. Routing both through one `ClientChannel` gives forward the tunnel's (stricter) behaviour, which is a silent improvement, not a regression — but it should be called out in the new module doc rather than left to be rediscovered.

NEW, lifting the fourth restated decision: `fn send_with_retry<W: Write>(w: &mut W, upstream: &mut UpstreamTls, from_pool: &mut bool, req: &[u8], ctx, ip, port, host, method, path, flow) -> Result<(), Refused>` — built from tunnel.rs:668-733 ≡ forward.rs:432-478. splits.other_observations:
**1. A real documentation defect, verified, worth fixing whether or not you split anything.** `src/sandbox/proxy/websocket.rs:965-978` is `relay_websocket`'s doc comment ("Relay an established bidirectional connection (a WebSocket) between the cage `client` and the `upstream`…"). It is followed at websocket.rs:979 by `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` and then at websocket.rs:980-983 by a *second* doc comment belonging to `TunnelObservers`, which is declared at websocket.rs:984. So the doc and the `#[allow]` both attach to `TunnelObservers` — a struct, for which `too_many_arguments` is meaningless — while the function they were written for sits undocumented 57 lines further down at websocket.rs:1041. That is exactly why `("sandbox/proxy/websocket.rs", "relay_websocket")` appears in the `UNDOCUMENTED_MODULE_ITEMS` allowlist at `src/docs_coverage.rs:935`. This happened when `TunnelObservers` was inserted between a function's doc and the function. The fix is three lines of movement — put websocket.rs:965-978 and the `#[allow]` back immediately above websocket.rs:1041 — after which docs_coverage.rs:935 must be deleted, or the staleness assertion at src/docs_coverage.rs:1082-1089 fires ("names items that are now documented or gone"). `relay_websocket` takes 7 parameters, and clippy's default `too_many_arguments` threshold warns at 8, so the `#[allow]` is not needed at all and can simply be dropped.

**2. Two modules I considered extracting from mod.rs and decided against.** `admit_absolute_form` and its three types (`RawRequest`:1807, `Plane`:1817, `AbsoluteForm`:1849, `admit_absolute_form`:1869-1983) is ~185 lines that reads as a candidate file. Leave it in mod.rs: its own doc (mod.rs:1874-1883) is the clearest statement in the directory of *why* the vocabulary exists — "the per-plane copy is precisely the mistake `wire::inspect_framing` exists to have fixed… steps 1, 3 and 4 were still copied, and now are not" — and putting it in a side file weakens the module doc's argument at exactly the point it is being made. Same call on the refusal writers (`refusal_body`:1673, `write_refusal`:1726, `refuse_unreadable_head`:1757, `unreadable_head_detail`:1788, `write_all_str`:1798, `invalid`:1985, `CONNECTION_CAP`:301, `UNREADABLE_HEAD`:324): ~130 lines, referenced by every plane, and mod.rs's reason table (mod.rs:89-111) is the documentation for them. Both stay.

**3. The one abstraction that would collapse several near-identical blocks and that I did NOT propose.** The relay tail — `relay_response_head` → empty-head `upstream-closed` → `set_status`/401 → `FramedBody` + `CountingReader` + `CaptureReader` + `pump_redacting`-or-`pump_to_eof` → the reuse triple — appears three times: tunnel.rs:795-899, forward.rs:515-607, cleartext.rs:267-295. A shared `relay_and_finish(...)` would fold all three. I left it out of the proposal because the three genuinely diverge in what they may announce (tunnel is the only one that offers `ClientLeg::MayReuse`, cleartext never masks and never parks) and folding them means a function with three behaviour flags — which is how a shared decision turns back into three decisions wearing one name. The two pieces of it that are *identical* in all three (`masks_reflection`, and the `set_status` + 401 pair) are in the `exchange.rs` proposal; the rest should stay written out.

**4. `tests.rs` (10,357 lines) and `bench.rs` (1,363, gated `#[cfg(test)] mod bench` at mod.rs:181-182) are out of scope but constrain every proposal here.** `tests.rs` is a flat `mod tests` whose only imports are `use super::ca::CertResolver;`, `use super::splice::{SpliceGuard, splice_copy};` and `use super::*;` (tests.rs:1-3). That single glob is why none of the eight splits above requires touching it — and it is also why every new child module must be glob-re-exported from mod.rs rather than merely declared. If someone later replaces the glob with explicit imports, the cost of all eight proposals rises sharply.

**5. Two `UpstreamPool` types.** `src/sandbox/proxy/pool.rs:85` (HTTP/1.1, take-and-return, `Mutex`, keyed by host+port+credential-ids) and `src/sandbox/proxy/h2mitm.rs:909` (HTTP/2, shared-not-returned, `RefCell`, keyed by credential-ids alone). Both are correct and the h2 one's doc (h2mitm.rs:897-907) explains the difference well. This is not a defect, but it is a hazard for any glob re-export, and it is worth knowing before proposal 8 is attempted.

**6. `ctx.rs` needs nothing.** At 998 lines (811 code) it is a struct with ~20 `with_*` builders and a set of observation chokepoints (`outcome`:393, `outcome_l7`:424, `push_log`:507, `set_status`:569, `register_flow`:372, `begin_capture`:340) that are deliberately the single funnel every plane records through — ctx.rs:145-152 and ctx.rs:161-166 both say so explicitly. Splitting the builders away from the chokepoints would put the fields and the one function that must see all of them in different files. Leave it.

**7. `wire.rs` needs nothing beyond the absorb.** 873 code lines, one concern, correctly named, tests already local (wire.rs:873-1667). After proposal 3 it is ~1,020 code lines and self-contained, and its `use super::*;` at wire.rs:7 could then be narrowed to explicit imports — a small follow-up that would make the directory's dependency shape readable from the import lines alone.

OVERLAP: DO THEY?

(1) store.rs ↔ storage.rs is a genuine two-way dependency, and the split between them is by IMPLEMENTATION TECHNOLOGY (nix vs btrfs), not by responsibility. "Where does sbx's data live" is one decision implemented in two mutually-recursive modules: storage.rs owns the pointer that redirects it (POINTER 96, read_pointer 103, write_pointer 196, clear_pointer 222, default_image 89, has_been_offered/mark_offered 236-251); store.rs owns the resolution that follows it (Layout::from_env 63, follow_volume 247, mounted_volume 267, data_dir_from 390). store.rs:252-253 and 268-271 call storage::read_pointer/ensure_mounted/state; store.rs:950 calls storage::on_btrfs. In the other direction storage.rs:989-1021 (`resolve_mkfs`) reaches back into store::Layout::from_env, store::resolve_nix, store::resolve_bwrap, store::LockTarget::global, store::revision_of and store::provision — i.e. into all four of store.rs's internal clusters. A third edge closes a triangle: storage.rs:1483 calls `crate::sandbox::reflink_verdict`, re-exported at src/sandbox/mod.rs:172 from projectstore.rs:443.

(2) store.rs vs projectstore.rs: NO overlap. store.rs owns the shared store and the host's own directories; projectstore.rs owns a per-project copy of it. Their only shared surface is the `Layout` type, and the seam (shared store read-only, project store written) is argued at length in the module doc and must be preserved.

(3) view.rs vs manage.rs: NO overlap. view.rs reads the RESOLVED configuration; manage.rs edits the RAW layer files. The one function that looks like a read in manage.rs — rules_in (1142) with its egress_rules_in/proc_rules_in wrappers — is deliberately paired with remove_rule_from, and its own doc says why ("navigating exactly as [`remove_rule_from`] does so the two cannot disagree about where a rule lives"). Moving it to view.rs would dissolve a stated seam.

NAME vs BOUNDARY, one line each:
 * store.rs — name claims "the nix store"; boundary held is "everything anchored on sbx's data directory, plus every host binary sbx execs, plus the nixpkgs channel pin, plus a GitHub reachability oracle". host_exec_verdict (641) is consumed by sandbox/resolver.rs:683 for plugin-declared programs and has nothing to do with a store.
 * storage.rs — name claims "storage"; boundary held is "a loop-mounted btrfs volume" PLUS two things unrelated to volumes: a general hardlink-preserving tree copier (759-926) and host-filesystem classification (1287-1421, whose `on_btrfs` is consumed by store.rs:950 and sandbox/launch.rs to pick a nix setting).
 * projectstore.rs — name and boundary agree exactly. The one misfit is the reflink capability probe (434-457), a filesystem question re-exported out of the module to serve storage.rs.
 * view.rs — name and boundary agree; the module has simply grown a second, self-contained consumer (the per-app roster and detail views) beside the baseline one.
 * manage.rs — name claims "management engine"; boundary held is four subjects at once: generic dotted-key editing, the `[network]`/`[proc]` posture matrix, atomic restricted file writing, and portable TOML fragment export/import.
splits.rationale:
store.rs is the one I would do first, and on its own it would be strongly recommended: 2,090 lines of code holding four subjects whose internal dependency graph is already one-directional and acyclic (layout ← engine, channel, provisioning; engine ← provisioning), and — verified item by item — the split requires ZERO visibility widenings. Every symbol crossing a proposed boundary (ensure, physical_path, resolve_nix_store, Layout) is already `pub(crate)`. Only two intra-doc links inside the file cross a new boundary (store.rs:1841 and store.rs:2024). All 217 external `store::Layout` references and all ~15 `crate::store::X` intra-doc links from other modules survive unchanged behind `pub(crate) use` re-exports in `store/mod.rs`, because rustdoc resolves re-exported paths. That is an unusually cheap split for an unusually clear payoff. The `channel` cluster in particular is a self-contained state machine (source → lock → pinned revision, with a seeded-not-baked rule spelled out over 60 lines of prose) that a reader currently has to find between the bwrap AppArmor logic and the nix-build argv assembly.

storage.rs, view.rs and manage.rs are worthwhile but not urgent — each is under the project's own 4,000-line pain threshold and each has a coherent module essay at the top. For them I propose only the extractions where the cluster is a DIFFERENT SUBJECT with its own consumers, not merely a large one: the tree copier and the filesystem classifier out of storage.rs, the per-app projection out of view.rs, the rule-verb posture matrix out of manage.rs. I deliberately do NOT propose splitting view.rs by "types here, projectors there": the file interleaves each view struct with the function that builds it (OpenView beside open_views, ServiceView beside service_views), which is a real property worth keeping, and separating them would make every change touch two files.

projectstore.rs is left alone. 670 lines of code, one subject, and its module doc carries the crate's most load-bearing argument (why the shared store stays byte-identical, why atomic rename per store path is sufficient, why no lock of sbx's own is needed). Splitting it would scatter that argument across files where no one reads it.

The one thing I would NOT do is merge store.rs and storage.rs to break their cycle. The cycle is real but its two directions are asymmetric: store→storage is a genuine layering (the data directory may live in a volume), while storage→store exists solely so `resolve_mkfs` can provision btrfs-progs. Isolating that one function into `storage/mkfs.rs` turns a diffuse cycle into a single named file, which is worth more than a merge that would produce a 3,600-line module.

CODE THAT BELONGS IN AN EXISTING MODULE:

GUARD MECHANICS THAT WILL BITE ANY OF THESE MOVES (all in src/docs_coverage.rs):
 * `UNDOCUMENTED_MODULE_ITEMS` (docs_coverage.rs:856-941) is keyed on (src-relative path, item name), and the test at :1081-1090 fails on a STALE entry as well as on a missing doc. Three entries in this scope are path-sensitive: `("storage.rs", "lock_image")` at :941, `("config/view.rs", "NetworkView")` at :891, `("sandbox/projectstore.rs", "acquire_shared_gc_lock")` at :928. Turning storage.rs or view.rs into a directory changes the first two keys to `storage/mod.rs` and `config/view/mod.rs`. `module_level_items` (:960) strips the `src/` prefix and skips only files named `tests.rs`/`*_tests.rs` — `mod.rs` is scanned like any other file.
 * The item regex at docs_coverage.rs:965 matches `fn|struct|enum|trait|union` only, so a bare `mod layout;` declaration needs no doc comment — and per mise.toml:97-98 it must NOT carry an outer `///` block, because that merges with the module's own header and moves the whole block's link resolution into the declaring module's scope. Give each new file an inner `//!` header instead; that is also what every existing multi-file module here (src/sandbox/*.rs, src/config/*.rs) does, and CLAUDE.md's documentation rule expects it.
 * `mise run rustdoc` is `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --document-private-items` (mise.toml:102), so links to PRIVATE items across the new boundaries do resolve — provided the path is spelled out (`super::channel::revision_from_metadata`) and the module is declared `pub(crate) mod`. The failure mode that will actually catch you is AMBIGUITY, which mise.toml:96 names outright: never give a new module the same name as an item re-exported beside it. That is the entire reason `src/store/provisioning.rs` is not called `provision.rs`.
 * None of these moves touches the docs-site guards (`every_cli_verb_has_a_reference_page`, `every_config_field_is_shown_in_the_guide`, `every_shipped_app_profile_is_in_the_catalogue`): no verb, config field or profile changes. And tests/ is CLI-level (it invokes the binary), so no integration test names a Rust path — `grep 'manage::\|view::' src/config/tests.rs` returns 0 too.

splits.rationale:
The duplication is measurable and the split is mechanical, but the two are separable and only one of them is urgent.

**The fixture duplication is the real finding, and it is bigger than the five files in scope.** `struct TmpDir` is declared in 21 files (src/testutil.rs plus every suite under tests/); `force_remove` is copy-pasted verbatim in 11 suites (tests/attach.rs:56, config.rs:53, detach.rs:59, doctor.rs:50, fs.rs:40, proc.rs:41, run.rs:88, sessions.rs:58, shell.rs:54, stop.rs:57, upgrade.rs:43); the `/proc/<pid>/stat` field-22 start-tick parser exists nine times under tests/ under four different names (app.rs:569 `start_ticks`, fs.rs:107 / logs.rs:50 / proc.rs:216 `read_start_ticks`, net.rs:1716/1830/2104/2248 inline, run.rs:8781 inline) against the one production copy at src/session.rs:752; and five suites (app.rs:36, config.rs:73, net.rs:37, path.rs:39, projects.rs:52) declare a near-identical `Fixture { proj, config_home, state_home, data_home }` whose `sbx()` sets the same three XDG variables plus `LC_ALL=C.UTF-8` / `env_remove("LANG")`. Inside tests/run.rs alone the launch preamble is written out by hand 76 times (`join(".sbx.toml")`), the capability probe 65 times (`run_in(project.path(), data.path(), &["true"])` followed by an eight-line `skip_incapable!` block differing only in the message), and the trust step 58 times (`&["trust", ".sbx.toml"]` plus its assertion). tests/common/mod.rs already exists, is `#[macro_use] mod common;`-ed by 16 suites, and carries `#![allow(dead_code)]` at line 12 precisely so a helper only one suite needs is not a warning in the others — the home is built and empty.

**That duplication is where the coverage gap actually lives.** Because the probe is retyped rather than called, it drifts. Two tests provision `nix:` packages in their *trusted* launch and carry no reachability gate at all: `a_trusted_audio_posture_binds_the_pulseaudio_socket_into_the_cage` (tests/run.rs:7495-7602, declares `alsautils = "nix:alsa-utils"` at 7516) and `a_trusted_audio_posture_equips_a_python_portaudio_tool` (7616-7746, declares `python312` and `uv` at 7641). Every comparable provisioning e2e in the file calls `cache_reachable()` and `skip_unreachable!`s; these two go red on a capable but offline host where the other 46 skip. A single `probe_or_skip!` helper makes that impossible by construction. The second gap is one of visibility: 83 of the 93 tests in tests/run.rs are gated, so on a host without userns/bwrap/nix the whole 9,373-line binary reports green having run ten tests — `run_detach_without_a_command_is_a_usage_error` (160-172), `a_malformed_one_shot_override_is_a_hard_error_and_does_not_launch` (333-378), `app_run_treats_a_subcommand_verb_as_an_app_name` (888-922), `the_quota_probe_reads_the_budget_that_governs_a_tool_install` (1178-1193) and the six `sbx_app_rm_*` tests (8577-8813). Nothing says which ten. The same shape in src/config/tests.rs: the field-by-field trust sweeps that a contributor adding a gated field must extend are driven by hand-written consts at 10368-10520, buried at line 10,400 of an 11,317-line file with no banner above them until 10793.

**The splits themselves buy less, and I want to be honest about that: not one of them adds a line of coverage.** src/sandbox/proxy/tests.rs is the weakest case — it is genuinely well ordered, it has one real shared harness at 99-639 rather than eight scattered ones, and `cargo test --bin sbx sandbox::proxy::tests::<filter>` already targets it. I propose splitting it only because its children map one-for-one onto the production submodules they exercise (ca.rs, cleartext.rs, forward.rs, tunnel.rs, websocket.rs, splice.rs, capture.rs, inject.rs, ssrf.rs, wire.rs are all real files beside it), so the split is a rename rather than a judgement, and because the file is now five times the size of the mod.rs it tests. src/config/tests.rs is the stronger case only because its clusters are not contiguous (secrets 7088-7358, overrides 7510-8326, secrets again 8328-10167) and no cut is possible without re-sequencing.

**tests/run.rs is the one where the split changes what a developer can do.** CLAUDE.md's own rule is "ALWAYS prefer targeted tests over the full suite", and today the finest grain available below `cargo test --test run` is a name filter — you cannot ask for "the egress e2es" or "the desktop e2es". .github/workflows/ci.yml:211-215 already runs `cargo test --test "$t"` per changed suite, so smaller suites give CI finer granularity for free. The cost is three more test binaries linking the full crate; cargo runs test targets one at a time (mise.toml:151 relies on this), so nothing about store contention or wall-clock on the cage job changes.

**tests/net.rs should be left alone.** 2,816 lines, 66 tests, zero skip macros, one coherent verb family, and it is the only suite in scope that already reads as a designed fixture. It should adopt the shared `Project` and the shared fake-session helper and stop there.

proposed_modules.purpose: Turn the existing sweep-helper module into the shared test-support root for every integration suite. It is already `#[macro_use] mod common;`-ed by 16 suites and already carries `#![allow(dead_code)]` (line 12) for exactly this case.
proposed_modules.moves: Nothing moves out. Added: `include!("../../src/testroot.rs")` (so `fixture_root()` has one definition per binary instead of 20), a `pub fn tmp_root() -> std::path::PathBuf { fixture_root() }` wrapper because the included `fn fixture_root` is private and cannot be `pub use`d, and the declarations `pub mod fixture; pub mod cage; pub mod session;`. The existing `walk`/`page_paths`/`oracle`/`sbx`/`stdout_of` (lines 23-110) stay put. The eight suites that do not yet include it — tests/app.rs, argv.rs, color.rs, logs.rs, net.rs, path.rs, session_logs.rs, trust.rs — gain `#[macro_use] mod common;` and drop their own `include!("../src/testroot.rs")`.
proposed_modules.risk: Ordering is load-bearing: `include!("../../src/testskip.rs")` at line 18 defines `macro_rules! skip_incapable` / `skip_unreachable`, which are textually scoped, so the three `pub mod` declarations MUST come after it or the submodules cannot use the macros. Both `include!`s must precede them for the same reason. No cyclic risk (tests/common depends on nothing). No rustdoc exposure — `tests/` is not documented by `cargo doc --no-deps`. src/docs_coverage.rs's `crate_and_test_sources()` (line 1108) does walk `tests/`, so the `a_paragraph_break_inside_a_doc_comment_is_written_as_one` guard applies to the new doc comments; carry blocks verbatim rather than re-wrapping them.

proposed_modules.purpose: The one temp-directory type and the one four-home project fixture, replacing 21 `struct TmpDir` declarations, 11 copies of `force_remove`, and five near-identical `struct Fixture`es.
proposed_modules.moves: `TmpDir` + `TAG_MAX` + `impl Drop` from tests/run.rs:49-84 (the tagged, length-budgeted variant — it is the strictest, because of the 108-byte `sun_path` cap the comment at 60-69 documents, so it is the one that must win); `force_remove` from tests/run.rs:86-104 (identical text to config.rs:51-68 and the nine others). A `pub struct Project` merged from tests/config.rs:73-190 and tests/net.rs:37-98: fields `proj`, `config_home`, `state_home`, `data_home`, `bind_dir`; methods `write_global`, `write_project`, `write_mise`, `write_profile`, `write_plugin`, `write_plugin_exec`, `source_plugin`, `bind_target`, `sbx`, `sbx_in`, `run`, `run_in`, `run_without_a_trust_store` (the last from net.rs:82-98). tests/config.rs and tests/net.rs then keep an alias `use common::fixture::Project as Fixture;` so their 198 call sites are untouched; tests/app.rs:36-64, path.rs:39-69 and projects.rs:52-80 collapse onto it too.
proposed_modules.risk: **This breaks a guard, and the guard must be re-based rather than relaxed.** src/testutil.rs:517-607 `every_fixture_root_is_the_shared_one` asserts `declaring >= 20` (line 604-607, message "only {declaring} files declare a fixture directory — has the sweep gone stale?"), where `declaring` counts files containing the literal `struct TmpDir`. There are exactly 21 today; after this consolidation there are 2 (src/testutil.rs and tests/common/fixture.rs) and the sweep fails on its own staleness precondition. The property it protects — no suite roots its fixtures anywhere but `fixture_root()` — is unchanged and in fact becomes trivially true; what has to change is the needle. Re-base it to count files that *reach* a fixture tree (`TmpDir::new(` / `Project::new(`), keep the existing rule that any file declaring `struct TmpDir` must contain `fixture_root()`, keep the `hardcoded` half (562-573) untouched, and rewrite the doc block at 493-516 to say what it now guards. Do not lower the number and leave the prose. Second risk: tests/config.rs's `TmpDir::new()` takes no tag while run.rs's takes one, so every call site in config.rs/net.rs/app.rs/path.rs/projects.rs needs a tag argument added — mechanical, and the compiler names every site. Third: tests/net.rs:29-32 uses `remove_dir_all` where everyone else uses `force_remove`; adopting `force_remove` there is strictly safer (it handles a 0555 nix store) and changes nothing net.rs relies on.

proposed_modules.purpose: The launch preamble and the host/remote reachability probes — the code that decides whether an e2e runs, said once. This is the file that closes the gate-drift gap.
proposed_modules.moves: From tests/run.rs: `sbx()` 13-29 (the `LC_ALL`/`LANG` and isolated-`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` builder), `run_in` 106-117, `app_in` 119-129, `app_in_args` 131-144, `sbx_in` 146-157, `KillOnDrop` 34-47, `cache_reachable` 1113-1123, `github_api_has_quota` 1125-1151, `quota_remaining` 1153-1175, `grpcb_in_reachable` 1195-1205, `postman_echo_reachable` 1207-1218, `transient_fetch_failure` 2037-2055, `wayland_socket` 2057-2072, `host_serves_notifications` 7999-8029, `cage_scope_tasks_max` 8031-8066, `cage_userns_ready` 8068-8117, `comm_of` 1933-1941, `comm_settles` 1942-1952, `read_loopback_until` 3725-3748, `free_loopback_port` 3750-3756. Plus two new macros that replace hand-written text: `probe_or_skip!(project, data, "<label>")` for the 65-fold block at run.rs:181-188 and its clones, and `need_cache!("<label>")` for the 46-fold `if !cache_reachable() { skip_unreachable!(…); return; }`. plan.overall_assessment:
Better factored than the line counts suggest; the proposals collectively overstate the problem by roughly half.

WHAT IS GENUINELY WELL DONE. The seams that matter are already cut and documented in prose, not folklore: Spec->argv is isolated; src/sandbox/projects.rs is kept out of launch on a stated criterion ("shares no state with the launch pipeline") precise enough to reuse as a test for other candidates; allowlist/grammar.rs says outright "the matching itself lives in [super]"; config/overrides.rs:45-48 names the boundary it refuses to cross; config/manage.rs rules_in explains why it is paired with remove_rule_from rather than filed with the readers. The guard suite is strong and doing real work: two non-recursive source scanners over src/cli (cli/mod.rs:966, help.rs:3727) that catch a dispatcher written to a new idiom; a docs-coverage list whose staleness half fails as loudly as its missing half (docs_coverage.rs:1082-1092); a fixture sweep asserting its own preconditions (testutil.rs:604-607). Several of the largest functions are correctly large -- build, run_admitted, cage_mounts, serve_tunneled_request, resolve, resolve_app are linear assemblies whose ordering is the security property, and six of the twelve engineers said so unprompted and declined to carve them.

WHAT IS NOT, in descending cost.

(1) About 40% of the "oversized module" problem is inline test modules, and the crate already has the fix in three places (proxy/mod.rs:2059, config/mod.rs:5841, openpgp/mod.rs:438), with docs_coverage.rs:995-997 skipping tests.rs / *_tests.rs whole. launch 2,708 lines of tests, proc_enforce 2,809, task+task_control 4,116, binds 2,968, allowlist 2,348 -- roughly 15,000 lines that can leave the production files at zero semantic cost. That nobody has done this is the largest single gap.

(2) A repeating documentation defect the guard was written for and is currently absorbing instead of catching. I verified four instances of the same failure -- a /// block severed from its item by a later insertion, so it renders on the wrong item and the intended one goes undocumented: config/mod.rs:503 (ResolvedApp's opening sentence swallowed into BundleProvision's doc), binds.rs:1460-1473 (build_spec's block sitting above write_atomic), allowlist/mod.rs:829-836 (EgressPolicy's paragraph rendering as Http2Host's; EgressPolicy at 955 has no doc at all), proxy/websocket.rs:965-979 (relay_websocket's doc AND its #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)] both landing on TunnelObservers, a struct). Three of the four are grandfathered in UNDOCUMENTED_MODULE_ITEMS (905, 857, 935) rather than fixed. The list's own doc says it can only shrink; it is not shrinking.

(3) Where duplication is real, it is in the two HTTP/1.1 proxy planes, and the proxy proposal's evidence is the best analysis in the set: three defects named in the codebase's own comments (forward.rs:83-89, h2mitm.rs:552-556, websocket.rs:786-789) each traced to a decision written out N times that drifted at one copy. That is a diagnosis worth acting on -- but not as part of a decomposition pass, for reasons in the ordering.

Sizes after step 2 alone, with no production code touched: launch 6,172; proc_enforce 2,940; task 2,320; binds 1,717; allowlist 1,741; task_control 1,741. Only launch is then still clearly oversized, and only it, proc_enforce, config/mod.rs and the two cli families genuinely warrant a directory.
plan.conflicts:
A. cli-config is wrong where cli-net is right, and only one of them looked. VERIFIED: both cli/mod.rs:966 (dispatch_heads) and help.rs:3727 (dispatched_alias_pairs) walk src/cli with a NON-recursive read_dir filtered to extension == "rs". cli-config proposes src/cli/config/mod.rs. config_cmd uses the scanned idiom verbatim (config.rs:30, `match args.first().and_then(|a| a.to_str()) {`) and ["config"] has child pages, so the assertion at cli/mod.rs:1113-1119 fails with "`sbx config` has subcommand pages but the scan found no dispatcher for it". cli-config asserts the opposite ("the split cannot fail it") because it checked docs_coverage and stopped. cli-net found the constraint and proposes the fix: keep src/cli/net.rs as the module root plus a src/cli/net/ directory. Resolution: cli-config adopts cli-net's shape; net lands first so the shape is precedent rather than argument. Verified safe for help-completion: completion_cmd does NOT use the idiom and ["completion"] has no child pages, so src/cli/completion/mod.rs is legal.

B. The same two proposals leave a latent hole neither fully owns. After net/ and completion/ exist, both scanners are structurally blind to two subtrees, and help.rs:3679 DISPATCHERS keys on bare filenames ("mod.rs"), which would collide across directories if the walk were made recursive. help-completion flagged the blindness; cli-net created it. Fix once, in the net step: make the walk recursive and key DISPATCHERS on the path relative to src/cli. Harmless today (I re-ran the scan: all 15 dispatcher pairs live in top-level files) and required before the third cli directory.

C. Three proposals each claim the test-module extraction as their own step one, and the ORDER between it and the production split is load-bearing in a way only two noticed. binds, task and allowlist all propose `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;`. allowlist states the dependency correctly: a child module sees its parent's private items, so tests extracted BEFORE a production split need no pub(super); tests extracted AFTER become siblings of the new modules and force widenings on every fixture they touch. Resolution: one cross-cutting extraction pass (step 2) covering all six files, landing before any production split, and each later step's pub(super) list is computed against sibling-tests.

D. Two proposals edit src/testutil.rs and only one sees the guard. launch promotes a test helper `resolved` there; test-suite consolidates 21 `struct TmpDir` declarations into 2. VERIFIED: testutil.rs:604-607 asserts `declaring >= 20` counting files containing the literal `struct TmpDir`, and there are exactly 21 today. The consolidation makes its own precondition fail. test-suite is right that the property survives (it becomes trivially true) and that the needle must be re-based, not the number lowered. Both edits land in step 3 so the guard is re-based once.

E. Nine docs_coverage keys are in flight across the plan and a partial rename fails the guard TWICE. Every entry is (src-relative path, item), so a file becoming a directory invalidates the key, and docs_coverage.rs:1082-1092 fails on a stale entry as well as on an undocumented item. Verified in-flight: 8 entries at proc_enforce.rs:920-927, 1 at task_control.rs:937, plus cli/completion.rs:861, config/view.rs:891, allowlist/mod.rs:857, storage.rs:940, binds.rs:905, proxy/websocket.rs:935. Three of those (905, 857, 935) should be DELETED in step 1 rather than re-keyed, because the underlying doc defect is fixable; completion.rs:861 likewise (write the missing /// on completion_cmd).

F. proxy-shape's exchange.rs collides with its own risk note. It proposes lifting ~200 lines shared by tunnel.rs and forward.rs, then concedes the move relocates about ten fail-closed refusal exits, in a directory whose own doc (mod.rs:1968-1983) calls the push_log/outcome split "the part most likely to drift under copying". Those two statements do not sit together in a decomposition pass. Resolution in the ordering: take the three small pieces, leave prepare_credentials to a dedicated change.

G. config-mod is a prerequisite for two later steps and none of the three says so. config-mod moves is_valid_app_name, is_valid_deb_url, is_valid_attr and six siblings behind pub(crate) use re-exports; cli-config's edit.rs and help-completion's values.rs both reach crate::config::* paths that only survive if those re-export lists are complete. Sequencing config/mod.rs before nothing that depends on it is not possible here (net and config come first for the shape), so the constraint is stated instead: the re-export lists are the contract, and the compiler enumerates every miss.

plan.leave_alone:
LEAVE ALONE, and the reasons differ. This section is where I disagree most with the submissions.

THE BIG FUNCTIONS THEIR OWN AUTHORS CORRECTLY REFUSED TO CARVE. Endorsed, and worth restating so nobody relitigates them.
- launch.rs build (3477-5204, 1,728 lines): one linear assembly whose ~40 locals converge on three consumers at the end (extra_cage_env, binds::build_spec, the LaunchGuard literal). Extracting the GUI-hole or provisioning blocks moves 8-10 values across a signature and splits the one surface sandbox/mod.rs:4-7 asks a security review to audit in one place. It moves whole into build.rs at ~2,700 lines and that is the correct answer.
- proxy/tunnel.rs serve_tunneled_request (53-927): 875 lines whose entire value is that one reader follows one request from head to close. The numbered step comments are the structure. Carving it into step_5/step_7 helpers destroys exactly what it is for.
- proc_enforce's supervisor (743-1030): one machine, one invariant (the single listener never blocks). Stays whole in mod.rs with the lifecycle that documents it.
- config/mod.rs fn resolve (1647-2593, 954 lines) and resolve_app (3277-3935, 666): a linear pass over ~60 accumulator locals. Every alternative is worse -- a ResolveState god-struct, or twenty &mut parameters threaded through sub-functions. It stays 954 lines under every proposal on the table and the config proposal is right to say so out loud.
- binds cage_mounts (368-707) and its in-cage destination constants: order IS the invariant (the OPT_DIR tmpfs is emitted before the config binds precisely so it shadows nothing), and the router's three-link mountpoint chain must stay visible on one screen with the constants declaring it.
- task run_admitted (685-950) and build_spec (990-1146): the ORDER is the security property -- the proc shim wraps innermost, redaction happens before anything is returned or logged.
- The proxy's two servers serve_cage and serve_host: the module header is one sustained argument about why these exist as a pair. Separating them separates the two halves of that argument.

MODULES THAT SHOULD NOT BE SPLIT AT ALL.
- src/sandbox/projectstore.rs (670 production lines). One subject, and it carries the crate's most load-bearing prose -- why the shared store stays byte-identical, why atomic rename per store path suffices, why no lock of sbx's own is needed. Splitting scatters that argument where nobody reads it.
- src/sandbox/fsmask.rs (622 production). One pipeline whose every stage shares Expanded/Masked/Decoys. There is no cut that does not bisect a data structure. The only self-contained piece is a 70-line git-index parser, which is not worth a file.
- src/sandbox/fhs.rs (400 production). A straight-line sequence of realise() calls where the comments are the content and the ordering carries meaning.
- src/sandbox/taskpool.rs, task_shim.rs. One subject each; task_shim is a format! template plus a nine-line writer, and separating a generated script's text from the function that writes it is pure loss.
- src/allowlist/grammar.rs. Already the parse seam, and says so in its header.
- src/sandbox/proxy/wire.rs and ctx.rs. wire is correctly named and cohesive; ctx's builders and its observation chokepoints must stay in one file because the chokepoints are the single funnel every plane records through and they need to see all the fields.
- tests/net.rs (2,816 lines, 66 tests, zero skip macros). The only suite in scope that already reads as a designed fixture. It adopts the shared Project in step 3 and stops.

SPLITS I AM REJECTING OUTRIGHT.
- allowlist beyond tests.rs. Step 2 takes it from 4,089 to 1,741 -- smaller than proxy/mod.rs, which nobody proposes splitting. The four production modules would put impl Rule in two files and impl RuleKind in two, fragmenting impl Ports and impl Methods for a render cluster of ~100 lines. The proposal half-concedes this about render.rs; the same logic finishes the argument for the other three. Take the tests, keep the module.
- src/sandbox/proxy/tests/ and src/config/tests/ subdivision. proxy/tests.rs is 10,357 lines of genuinely well-ordered tests behind one real 540-line harness, and cargo test --bin sbx sandbox::proxy::tests::<filter> already targets it. The only thing wrong with it is its size, which is not a defect. config/tests.rs is the better case (its clusters are non-contiguous, so any cut is a re-sequencing) but its sharpest hazard is a deliberate shadowing shim at tests.rs:60-77 whose mis-import would silently compile 46 call sites against the wrong function -- the one failure mode in this whole plan the compiler cannot catch. Neither is worth that risk before everything above is done.
- tests/run.rs split into run_desktop/run_egress/run_tools. Deferred, not rejected. The finer granularity is real and CI already runs per-suite, but it adds three test binaries and two hardcoded suite lists (mise.toml:123, cage.yml:287, held character-identical by a guard) for zero coverage change. Step 3 captures the part that actually matters -- the fixture consolidation and the two ungated audio e2es.
- Merging store.rs with storage.rs; merging config's two trust gates (scope_is_gated vs open_rule_write); merging store::host_exec_verdict with config::safety::verdict; folding config/override_apply into overrides.rs. All four would dissolve a seam the code argues for in place.
- proxy's prepare_credentials extraction, per conflict F -- worth doing, not worth doing here.
- Sharding help.rs's PAGES by namespace, and factoring binds' two prebuilt walks behind a run_command: bool (which would put 'gc must never run the resolve command or touch the network' behind a boolean argument).

ONE THING NOBODY PROPOSED THAT IS WORTH MORE THAN HALF THIS LIST. The UNDOCUMENTED_MODULE_ITEMS list at docs_coverage.rs:856-943 is absorbing a recurring defect rather than catching it -- four verified instances of the same severed-doc-block failure, three of them grandfathered. The guard's own doc says the list can only shrink. Step 1 removes four entries; a follow-up should audit the remaining ~80 for the same pattern, because every one of them is either a real doc that needs writing or a block that has silently drifted onto the wrong item.

sweeps.summary: I read every file in src/cli (24 files, ~31k lines) plus the shared helpers they import from src/main.rs (`resolve_session_target`, `split_scope`, `split_session_flags`, `split_one_rule`, `config_cwd`, `interval_seconds`, `persist_egress_rule`/`persist_proc_rule`, `open_rule_write`) and src/cli/mod.rs (`reject_extra`, `parse_one_name`/`one_name`, `parse_one_file`/`one_file`, `keep_replaced_file`, `settings_dropped_by`). The per-verb argument grammars are in good shape — the genuinely repeated grammars (`<verb> <name> [switch]`, `<verb> <file> [switch]`, the scope/session flag split) already have pure, unit-tested shared parsers, and the twin-module seams the code explicitly documents (`removal_words`, the `Spec`-style separation of parse from I/O) are deliberate and worth keeping. What is duplicated is the *plumbing between* the parser and the work: resolving the data directory, resolving the cwd, opening the session registry, composing the `--session` pid filters, and reporting a rule write. Those are copied 4–28 times each and have already drifted into five different wordings for "cannot find the data directory" and four for "cannot serialize". Two whole functions in the fragment-import path (`keep_replaced_bundles`/`keep_replaced_groups` and their renderers) are byte-identical apart from one noun, and the code comment at net.rs:2454 already admits it. I also found ~600 lines of copy-pasted `ConfigView` test fixtures in config.rs. I did not find hand-rolled table rendering worth consolidating: the `style::print_table`/`render_table` pair exists and the remaining hand-rolled listings (app.rs:1337, net.rs:1218, net.rs:2678) build into a `String` with a two-space indent and per-cell hues that `print_table` deliberately does not offer, so folding them would change output for a small win — leave those alone.

findings.title: "Resolve the data directory or fail" is written 28 times in src/cli, in five different wordings
findings.also_at: src/cli/task.rs:176 (the existing helper), src/cli/plugins.rs:391,842,1100,1179,1218,1306,1385,1481,1787,1898,2016,2100; src/cli/proc.rs:481,538,623,732; src/cli/logs.rs:93,564; src/cli/session.rs:70,512; src/cli/app.rs:1053,1394,1876; src/cli/store.rs:96; src/cli/search.rs:21; src/cli/upgrade.rs:183
findings.description: The same six-line gesture appears 28 times, with five separate texts for one failure. task.rs:176 already extracted it: `fn layout_or_fail() -> Result<store::Layout, ExitCode> { store::Layout::from_env().ok_or_else(|| { diag::error("sbx: cannot resolve the data directory (no $SBX_DATA_DIR, $XDG_DATA_HOME or $HOME)."); ExitCode::FAILURE }) }`. proc.rs:481-487 copies that text verbatim: `let Some(layout) = store::Layout::from_env() else { diag::error("sbx: cannot resolve the data directory (no $SBX_DATA_DIR, $XDG_DATA_HOME or $HOME).",); return ExitCode::FAILURE; };` — as do logs.rs:93, logs.rs:564, proc.rs:538/623/732, session.rs:70/512, search.rs:21, upgrade.rs:183 (11 sites). plugins.rs:622-627 says something else for the same condition: `let Some(layout) = store::Layout::from_env() else { diag::error("sbx: cannot locate the data directory (set $SBX_DATA_DIR, $XDG_DATA_HOME or $HOME)",); return ExitCode::FAILURE; };` — repeated at 13 sites in that file (391 and 2100 through `load_plugin_registry()`). app.rs:1053-1058 has a third: `"sbx: cannot locate sbx's data directory (set $SBX_DATA_DIR, $XDG_DATA_HOME or $HOME)"`. app.rs:1394-1397 and app.rs:1876-1879 have a fourth, verb-tagged and with no remedy at all: `diag::error("sbx: app show: cannot locate sbx's data directory.");`. store.rs:96-99 has a fifth: `diag::error("sbx store: cannot locate sbx's data directory.");`.
findings.impact: The drift has already happened: one condition, five messages, two of which (app.rs:1395, app.rs:1877, store.rs:97) do not tell the user which variables to set. Every future change to that remedy sentence is 28 edits, and the odds of catching all five variants with one grep are low — `grep 'cannot resolve the data directory'` finds 11 of the 28. Each copy is also 6 lines of noise at the head of a handler.
findings.fix: Move `layout_or_fail` from src/cli/task.rs:176-183 to src/main.rs, beside `config_cwd` (main.rs:266) and `resolve_session_target` (main.rs:86) — the crate root is already the documented home for cross-family CLI plumbing (see the module doc at src/cli/config.rs:5-8). Make it `pub(crate)`, give it a doc comment, and keep the `cannot resolve …` wording (the majority, and the only one that names the variables). Replace all 27 inline blocks with `let layout = layout_or_fail()?;` in `-> Result<_, ExitCode>` helpers or `let layout = match layout_or_fail() { Ok(l) => l, Err(c) => return c };` in `-> ExitCode` handlers. For plugins.rs:391 and 2100 the value is `load_plugin_registry()`; give that function the same treatment (`fn load_plugin_registry() -> Result<(store::Layout, PluginRegistry, Vec<String>), ExitCode>` calling `layout_or_fail()?`). Two guard consequences to carry: delete the `("cli/task.rs", "layout_or_fail")` entry from `UNDOCUMENTED_MODULE_ITEMS` in src/docs_coverage.rs:884 (the moved function is documented), and re-check any integration test asserting the `cannot locate` phrasing.

findings.title: `keep_replaced_bundles`/`keep_replaced_groups` and their renderers are the same functions with one noun swapped
findings.description: `diff` of bundle.rs:354-385 against net.rs:2502-2533 is four hunks: the fn name, and the noun "bundle" vs "egress group" in two format strings. 26 of 32 lines are byte-identical, including `const NAMED: usize = 3;`, the `dropped.is_empty()` early return, the `.take(NAMED).map(|l| format!("`{l}`"))` join, the `saturating_sub(NAMED)` " (and {rest} more)" tail, and the `if dropped.len() == 1 { "1 line".to_string() } else { format!("{} lines", dropped.len()) }` pluralization. The `keep_replaced_*` pair is the same story: `diff` of bundle.rs:307-348 against net.rs:2456-2497 is seven hunks — the signature, `config::bundles()` vs `config::net_groups()`, the `one(...)` exporter closure, the `.bundle.replaced` vs `.group.replaced` suffix, the noun in one error, and the renderer call. The `if !force { return Ok(Vec::new()); }` guard, the `config_path.parent()` guard, the `declared.get(name)` "added, not replaced" skip, the `before == after` skip, and the `crate::cli::keep_replaced_file(&kept, before.as_bytes()).map_err(...)` call are identical. net.rs:2454 already names the duplication in prose: "The bundle importer does the same thing for the same reason — see `cli::bundle::keep_replaced_bundles`." The two callers (bundle.rs:393-483 `bundle_import`, net.rs:2541-2643 `net_groups_import`) then repeat a third copy of the same 20-line shape: cwd → `config::manage::scope_path(&Scope::Global, &cwd)` → `keep_replaced_*` → import → `for note in &replaced { diag::warn(note); }` → the identical added/overwritten summary (bundle.rs:447-457 vs net.rs:2595-2605, byte-identical).
findings.impact: ~150 lines of twinned code. The halves this operation already shares (`keep_replaced_file`, `settings_dropped_by`) live in cli/mod.rs, so the split is arbitrary: any change to the overwrite warning's shape — the NAMED cap, the pluralization, the "differed only in layout" case — is two edits in two files, and the wording is user-visible so a missed one is a visible inconsistency. The line-wrap already differs between the two copies of the same sentence.
findings.fix: In src/cli/mod.rs, beside `keep_replaced_file` (mod.rs:234) and `settings_dropped_by` (mod.rs:273): add `pub(crate) fn render_replaced_fragment(noun: &str, name: &str, dropped: &[String], kept: &Path) -> String` — the body of bundle.rs:354-385 with `"replaced {noun} `{name}`, …"`. Add `pub(crate) fn keep_replaced_fragments<T>(config_path: &Path, incoming: &BTreeMap<String, T>, declared: &BTreeMap<String, T>, force: bool, noun: &str, suffix: &str, export_one: impl Fn(&str, &T) -> Result<String, String>) -> Result<Vec<String>, String>` — the body of bundle.rs:307-348, calling `render_replaced_fragment`. Delete bundle.rs:307-385 and net.rs:2456-2533; each caller keeps only its own `config::bundles()` / `config::net_groups()` lookup, its `"bundle"`/`"egress group"` noun, its `"bundle"`/`"group"` suffix, and its exporter closure (`export_bundles` returns `Result`, `export_net_groups` returns `String` — wrap the latter in `Ok`). Move the two existing renderer tests (bundle.rs:601-616, net.rs:3536-3548) to mod.rs and parameterize them by noun. Also hoist the added/overwritten summary (bundle.rs:447-457, net.rs:2595-2605) as `pub(crate) fn import_summary(added: &[String], overwritten: &[String]) -> String`. Nothing here is an intra-doc link target, so rustdoc is unaffected; the net.rs:2454 prose reference to `cli::bundle::keep_replaced_bundles` must be rewritten to point at the shared helper.
findings.verifier_note: Three corrections. (1) The proposed `noun` parameter is not enough: the error path says "cannot keep the bundle/group being replaced" while the warning says "replaced bundle/egress group" — two different tokens ('group' vs 'egress group'). The proposed signature happens to carry both (`noun` for the render, `suffix` for the file name), so the error must be built from `suffix`, not `noun`, or one of the two messages changes wording. (2) Line-range nits: the import summary block is bundle.rs:448-459 vs net.rs:2596-2607 (verified `let mut parts = Vec::new();` at bundle.rs:448 and net.rs:2596), not 447-457/2595-2605; the two renderer tests are bundle.rs:599-620 and net.rs:3533-3551 — the cited numbers are the `render_replaced_*` calls inside them. (3) The `import_summary` hoist is the weakest part of the fix: it is ~12 lines over two different outcome types, and the `println!` around it differs ("imported {} bundle(s)" vs "imported {} egress group(s)"), so it saves little; the `keep_replaced_fragments` + `render_replaced_fragment` extraction is where the ~150 lines actually collapse.
findings.verifier_reason: Line ranges confirmed by grep -n: bundle.rs:307 `fn keep_replaced_bundles(`, bundle.rs:354 `fn render_replaced_bundle(...)`, bundle.rs:393 `fn bundle_import(...)`; net.rs:2456 `fn keep_replaced_groups(`, net.rs:2502 `fn render_replaced_group(...)`, net.rs:2541 `fn net_groups_import(...)`. Reading both bodies confirms the described sameness: identical `if !force { return Ok(Vec::new()); }`, `config_path.parent()` guard, `declared.get(name)` "added, not replaced" skip, `before == after` skip, `crate::cli::keep_replaced_file(&kept, before.as_bytes()).map_err(…)`, and identical renderers down to `const NAMED: usize = 3;`, the `.take(NAMED).map(|l| format!("`{l}`"))` join, `saturating_sub(NAMED)`, the " (and {rest} more)" tail and the 1-line/N-lines pluralization; only the noun differs in the two format strings, and the line-wrap of the same sentence does differ between the copies.
